Adder Lane was minor avenue of hard-packed earth and gravel in the Dock Ward of Waterdeep.

This road ran from northwest to southeast, extending off of the Fishgut Court and terminating at an intersection with Gut Alley. Not far from its opening at Fishgut Court, the lane was intersected by Wastrel Alley.

The Adder Peaks were located along the southern border of Chessenta along the northeastern edge of the Chondalwood. Both the Winding River and Adder River originated in the Adder Peaks.

entities.description:
The Adder River ran south to north from the Adder Peaks to empty into the Bay of Chessenta through the Adder Swamp.

The Adder River was described as being a wide, slow flowing river with muddy water. Lush vegetation surrounded the river for its entire length, hiding plenty of dangerous snakes.

A community of werecrocodiles was also known to inhabit its waters near the Adder Swamp.

entities.name: Adder Swamp
entities.description:
The Adder Swamp, sometimes spelled Adderswamp, was a dangerous expanse of lycanthrope-infested marshland that surrounded the Adder River delta in Chessenta.

The swamp was murky and infested with insects and vermin. Like the Adder River, the Adder Swamp was known for its large snake population. It was also one of the few rare places along the entire coast of Chessenta where sailors would not moor their boats.

It was a salt marsh notable for its production of salt.

Following the Spellplague and the various catastrophes that befell Chessenta, the Adder Swamp greatly expanded to cover much of the western coast of the Bay of Chessenta.

entities.name: Adhe Wood
entities.description:
Adhe Wood was a forest located in the Vast infested with arachnid monsters.

It lay south of the Earthfast Mountains, between the North Road and the Tsurlar Forest, north-east of the hamlet of Sevenecho.

The forest was old, dense, and overgrown, and the trunks of its trees stood very close together. Most of these were duskwoods and shadowtops, while felsuls and oaks were found on the southern edge. The tallest trees grew over 80 feet (24 meters) tall. As a result, the depths of Adhe Wood were kept in eternal darkness.

Deep in Adhe Wood were found large numbers of ettercaps and spiders. These spiders could be of any size or variety, and most possessed bizarre magical powers and mutations, such as hooked, slashing claws or stinging tails. They were exceedingly vicious and constantly hunted both each other and those who ventured into the forest.

entities.name: Al-Adib River
entities.description:
Al-Adib River, also known as the "River of Courtesy," wound itself through southwestern Zakhara for more than 100 miles (161 km) across the plains of the High Desert to the coast of the Golden Gulf.

Al-Adib was filled with rancid water, courtesy of centuries of local humans using it as their dumping ground. This practice was forbidden by Sheikh Ali al-Hadd, ruler of Tajar, but most of the local peasants ignored his decree and continued filling the river with soiled clothing, vegetable matter, and even an occasional donkey carcass. Some areas of the river were so congested with garbage that dim-witted battan fish lurking just an inch beneath the surface could not be seen, making it one of the least attractive rivers in the Land of Fate.

The western portion of Al-Adib was criss-crossed by a web of small tributaries, many only a few inches deep. Deeper tributaries played home to several variety of battan fish that were easily caught and delicious. Salty mineral deposits made the water here undrinkable, even though human pollution was considerably less than the eastern portions of the river.

Western Al-Adib was dotted with slum settlements. The harbors where Al-Adib emptied into the Golden Gulf near Tajar were typically jammed with merchant ships and vessels for aristocrats. Merchants here were extremely wary of beggars and usually killed on site unless a bribe of a silver piece was offered.

entities.description:
Admiral's Way was a dockside street in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate.

Admiral's Way was located in the Eastway, a single city block south of Sailor's Crossing plaza. The Low Lantern festhall was docked at the eastern end of Admiral's Way in the 15 century DR.

In the summer of the , on Kythorn 19, the Sailor's Crossing plaza became a scene of a grizzly murder, located just within earshot of Admiral's Way. A puking human male was reported being on Admiral's Way shortly after the murder took place, but the detective missed the opportunity to interrogate the likely witness.

entities.description:
Adoivaealumanth () was a small holy city in the Aryselmalyr Empire that over time fell to ruin, leaving only its grand temple to Deep Sashelas.

This city was located beneath the Sea of Fallen Stars,

The various buildings within Adoivaealumanth were constructed of various types of coral. After the city was abandoned, with no one to tend to them the buildings grew into massive coral reefs, sealing up the doorways and windows they once had.

Having been founded for the purposes of religious devotion, neither trade nor any political activities were conducted in the holy city of Adoivaealumanth.

entities.name: Adventurer Mart
entities.description:
The Adventurer Mart was a shop found within Waukeen's Promenade in the Center District of Athkatla during the 14 century DR. Although they were typically looked down upon in most parts of the city, this shop catered to adventurers, selling magical items, weapons, armor and spellcasting supplies. In defiance of the Cowled Wizards, the Adventurer Mart also had a merchant that sold magical scrolls.

The store was located in the western part of Waukeen's Promenade. It was the closest store to the location where Abdel Adrian escaped from the dungeon of Jon Irenicus.

The outer structure of the store was a essentially a large block of stone with a single wooden door. It was surrounded by two stone staircases, which lead up to the other stores in the western part of the promenade.

The Adventurer Mart was divide into two floors: the entry floor and the top floor. The entry floor was patrolled by a guard, and contained the desk of the owner, Ribald Barterman. This floor displayed several booths of armor, weapons, and tools (such as shovels and pickaxes). There was also a giant musical harp and several filled bookcases.

entities.name: Adventurer's Guild
entities.description:
The Adventurer's Guild was an adventuring organization operating in the city of Neverwinter during the late 15 century DR. It served as a recruitment and coordination center for adventurers, mercenaries, explorers, and freelance agents acting in service to the city's restoration and defense.

The Adventurer's Guild functioned as one of the primary organizations responsible for coordinating independent adventurers within Neverwinter following the devastation caused by the eruption of Mount Hotenow in 1451 DR. Adventurers arriving in the city commonly reported to the guild after entering the Protector's Enclave, where they received assignments involving military operations, monster eradication, exploration, reconnaissance, and regional security. The guild also served as a logistical and training center. Merchants, craftsmen, and mercenary suppliers provided equipment, magical items, armor, weapons, and provisions to adventurers operating under the guild's authority.

The Adventurer's Guild was located within the Protector's Enclave, on the Deekin Street near the the Seven Suns Coster Market. It operated out of the building formerly occupied by the Trade of Blades (though it was completely restructured). Within its halls was a grand library lounge for wizards and scholars, a modest chapel for clerics and paladins, and a trophy room where adventurers gathered to share stories over a roasting boar. For those fascinated by tales of the past, the Acolytes of History established themselves within the second-floor archives, offering knowledge and lore concerning Neverwinter's history. The wizards of the Adventurer's Guild even crafted a special demiplane where adventurers could safely train their techniques and test their mettle.

The guildhall acted as a central gathering place for adventurers operating throughout Neverwinter and the surrounding Sword Coast North.

entities.name: Adventurers' Guild House
entities.description:
The Adventurers' Guild House was the guildhall for the Adventurers' Guild of Sphur Upra. It also served as one of the city's inns.

The building was located in the Shadow District of the gloaming city of Sphur Upra.

This inn was exceptionally welcoming to visitors from the Material Plane, as the Guild's members were always eager to hear tales of adventure from other realms. Guildmembers were also anxious to share their own tales and planned quests of the Shadow Plane to guests and readily shared drinks and congratulatory back-slaps.

entities.name: Aeaea
entities.description:
Aeaea was the divine realm of Hecate, Olympian goddess of magic.

Hecate was one of the few powers who maintained a realm on more than one plane. Her primary domain was the 3 layer of the Gray Wastes, Pluton, and a smaller, identically named realm was located in Baator, originally on the 4 layer of Phlegethos and later moved to the 3 layer of Minauros. She spent time in both realms, and it was completely unknown why she had two. It was speculated that she drew power from both planes to empower her worshipers, or given the residents of Plutonian Aeaea swore she never left, that without her power to cohere it the realm ceased existence until she returned.

In any case, Aeaea was a mysterious and enigmatic realm. It was a place of hatred and terror, as was to be expected of the lower planes, but intermingled with love and beauty. It teemed with omens and signs, with almost everything symbolizing something else. Fates could be read in the acts of beasts or movements of plants, and a sign of doom for one could be a portent of unearned success for another. Overall Aeaea always conveyed the feeling that its peace was false, like the calm before the storm or the stillness in the eye of a hurricane, that the worst was still yet to come.

In Hecate's hilly, grove-dotted realm the night was ceaseless, and yet not infinite. Nights had clear beginnings and endings, indicated by a sense of closure across the realm, an approximately hour long interim of pitch blackness, and the new night visibly rising from the east. The kind of night Aeaea experienced was correctly assumed by most residents to be dependent on Hecate's whims and mood, and could vary greatly. Weather ranged from clear skies, drifting warm breezes and gentle rains (rare in Hades), downpours, and raging storms with crackling, deathly thunder.
entities.short_description: Aeaea was the divine realm of Hecate, Olympian goddess of magic.

entities.name: Aearee-Krocaa
entities.description:
The Aearee-Krocaa was an aearee culture and one of the Aearee Empires during the Days of Thunder.

Around , on Mount Havraquoar somewhere in the west of Faerûn, the Aearee-Krocaa founded Viakoo, a grand aerie and home-nest that was to be the capital of their nation.

Around , a thousand Aearee-Krocaa were slain by a much smaller force of lammasu. The Aearee-Krocaa later experimented on domesticated landwyrms to create the first winged wyrms, or wyverns as the aearee named them. They supported their forces with wyvern armies, rapidly expanding the Aearee-Krocaa empire.

Finally, around , dragons all around Faerûn swarmed, forming the first Flight of Dragons. They assaulted the aearee everywhere, in the skies, on the land, and even underground. Descending on Viakoo from the skies, they completed razed it. This marked the fall of the Aearee Empires, the rise of the Time of Dragons, and the beginning of the Dawn Ages.

entities.name: Aebrynis
entities.description:
Aebrynis was a world ruled by the inheritors of divine bloodlines in constant struggle with each other and against powerful creatures tainted by evil.

Portals connecting Aebrynis from other worlds were few and far between, so it was considered a backwater by planewalkers. However, limited planar travel through various other means between Aebrynis and Faerûn, Kara-Tur, and the Rock of Bral were not unknown.

The world was known to Faerûnian scholars primarily in connection with Sera, its native goddess of commerce, who was working together with Waukeen and other like-minded deities to maintain the grand realm of the Marketplace Eternal in the Outlands.

Like Toril, Aebrynis had one sun and one moon.

entities.name: Aefarn
entities.description:
Aefarn, better known as the House of Gold, was a major center of the worship of Abbathor, the dwarven god of greed, and served as a fortified vault wherein his clergy hid their massive wealth. It contained possibly the greatest assemblage of treasure to have ever existed on Toril.

The temple complex lay underground deep beneath Turnback Mountain

The fortified cavern complex which served as the temple had been carved from the rock long ago by a mighty red dragon, and as of the mid-to-late 14 century DR, the caverns were completely covered in gold-leaf and studded with precious stones and gems. The vast wealth of Abbathor's worshipers was housed in heavily-defended chambers.

Each of Abbathor's priests was responsible for defending the chambers which contained their own share of the wealth, meaning that any attackers would crash against a myriad of heavily trapped fortresses-within-fortresses as they attempted to move through the complex. Defense of the temple proper was the primary duty of the Three Coinlords, a triumvirate of the most senior priests who were the formal rulers of Aefarn.

entities.name: Aefindar Ultokhumden
entities.description:
Aefindar Ultokhumden, also known as the Trademoot of Golden Fortune, was a large cathedral dedicated to Vergadain in the city of Eartheart. It doubled as the city's central marketplace and the administrative center of Eartheart's ministry of trade and commerce.

This cathedral was located in the center of Eartheart, on the rim of the Great Rift.

This cathedral was like a fortress and had exterior walls that were made of granite, but plated in gold that was so regularly polished that it shined intensely.

The great hall of this temple acted as a marketplace, while its upper chambers was where Eartheart's ministry of trade and commerce were housed. The lower levels of Aefindar housed much of Eartheart's wealth, as well as three grand chapels dedicated to Vergadain.

entities.name: Aelinthaldaar
entities.description:
Aelinthaldaar was the capital city of Illefarn, an ancient elven civilization in northwest Faerûn. The city was located where Waterdeep would later stand.

The city was founded circa and stood for some seven thousand years.

However, the elves destroyed their own city in when they retreated to Evermeet. The coronal of Illefarn ordered the whole city razed with elven high magic, leaving very little behind to indicate it had ever been there.

The elves of Aelinthaldaar created a magical effect, or mythal, known as the Melairshield, which prevented the plateau from collapsing, regardless of activities below the surface. It remained in effect into the 14 century DR.

entities.name: Aelor
entities.description:
Aelor was a short-lived prospector settlement located within the Lilit Pass of the Vilhon Reach, later turned into a city-state.

Aelor neighbored Daroush, the location of the infamous gold mines. Amah was the closest city to Aelor, located to the south on the shores of the Vilhon Reach and the town of Xorhun to the north.

Aelor was settled in 277 DR, practically overnight, following a discovery of seemingly rich gold vein. However, this proved to be untrue and gold deposits were exhausted only five year later. By 282 DR, most industrious prospects of Aelor suffered financials losses and by 284 DR, Aelor became a ghost town of abandoned buildings. Most inhabitants of Aelor moved on to the city Amah.

By 1370 DR, Amah returned to life as a small independent city-state. The neighboring Hlondeth had no interest in expansion and the takeover of Amah. Dediana Extaminos, the yuan-ti ruler of Hlondeth, was focused on effective rulership of her domain, however if possibility to take over Amah or other neighboring city-states arose, she was willing to consider expansion.

entities.description:
Mount Aergurl, known earlier as The Sleeper In The Sunrise, was a mountain in the Vast in north Faerûn. It lay within the Giantspike Mountains, a part of the Earthspur Mountains, and was due east of the village of Maskyr's Eye.

Described as a long rising peak, down Aergurl's slope ran a creek that had carved a high cleft. Though hazardous, this cleft formed a pass through the mountains, leading to high chilly valleys and ultimately the Glacier of the White Worm.

The pass was little known to humans in the mid–14 century DR. The folk of Maskyr's Eye were aware of it, but did not talk about it to outsiders, but their hunters warned of an unnatural cold beyond the Sleeper.

The local dwarves had a legend of how the dwarf hero Aurgus killed a remorhaz single-handedly in the mountain pass.

entities.name: Aerhiot's Field
entities.description:
Aerhiot's Field was a farm somewhere in Faerûn during the mid–8 century DR.

There was a sunken road between Aerhiot's Field and the neighboring Salopar's Field. The hedges outside both fields had overgrown into the ditch-level path to such a degree that they formed a gloomy tunnel-like space underneath their intertwined branches.

Squirrels and birds darted along the path every time someone used it.

In the , while traversing the path between Aerhiot's Field and Salopar's Field, the farmer Nuglar fell prey to the Slayer, a mysterious, ethereal apparition, which slew him and his three oxen, leaving nothing but dust behind.
entities.short_description: Aerhiot's Field was a farm somewhere in Faerûn during the mid–8 century DR.

entities.name: Aerie
entities.description:
The Aerie was the divine realm of the elven goddess of air, weather and avians, Aerdrie Faenya, which she shared with Syranita, goddess of the aarakocra. Among the latter the place was known as Whistledge.

In the Great Wheel cosmology, the Aerie could shift according to their deities' whims between the joint realm of the Seldarine in Arvandor and the homestead of more chaotic-minded elven petitioners, Alfheim. The former was part of Arborea's first layer (also called Arvandor); the latter lay in Ysgard's first layer (also named Ysgard).

In the World Tree cosmology, the realm was located within the plane of Arvandor.

In either case, it floated above the breathtaking landscapes inhabited by the earth-bound petitioners.
entities.short_description: The Aerie was the divine realm of the elven goddess of air, weather and avians, Aerdrie Faenya, which she shared with Syranita, goddess of the aarakocra. Among the latter the place was known as Whistledge.

entities.name: Aerie of the Snow Eagles
entities.description:
The Aerie of the Snow Eagles was the only known large settlement of the avariel left on Toril. A citadel made of glassteeled crystal, it was located near the eastern edge of the Great Glacier, atop the sheared peak of Mount Sundabar, and part of the northernmost Icerim Mountains.

The avariel community of Mount Sundabar, including nests on the mountains flanks, was loosely governed by Winged Father Aquilan Greatspan, who had as of led the community for near five centuries, and seen the avariel survive, if not exactly prosper, amidst the ruins of the Ice Kingdom of Dareth.

Before the First Flowering, the avariel, who had left Faerie before many of the rest of their elf kin, found themselves the frequent victims of dragon attacks. The dragons, who favored avariel flesh, eventually drove the avariel to the brink of extinction, forcing the survivors to live squalid lives as destitute nomads, unable to take flight for fear of being eaten. They slowly traveled east, hoping that their draconic foes would not find them.

Millennia passed and eventually a group of avariel nomads braved the climb up a remote and sheer mountain on the eastern fringe of Pelvuria. Curiously, the peak of the mountain was gone and instead they found a great plateau. Assuming that the plateau was made by a Netherese arcanist to create one of their enclaves, the avariel decided to settle. Thankfully for the elves, the realm of white dragons that had lived in the range had all been killed by a group of dwarves not long previous. Safe from their ancient foes and isolated from those far below them on the ground, the winged elves managed to prosper.

entities.name: Aerilpar Forest
entities.description:
The Aerilpar Forest, also known as the Wood of Dark Trees, both for its animated jungle and the dangerous beasts that prowled it, was located in Veldorn in the Shining South.

The Wood of Dark Trees was found between the Giant's Belt Mountains to the north and the Liontongue River to the south.

Among its more notable features was the Aerilpar Mound, also known as the Mound of the Sleepless.

True to its name, the trees of this steamy forest were evil. It was widely rumored that the trees were some kind of animated monster created by a foul wizard.

entities.description:
Aerynn's Street was a street found in the coastal town of Aithelar in Callidyrr on the Moonshae Isles in .

Aerynn's Street connected and ran perpendicular to Bottle Lane and Callidyrr Ride near the center of Aithelar. It intersected Aithe High Street midway along its length.

entities.name: Afyal
entities.description:
The kingdom's capital, Medina al-Afyal, was also its only real city. often bearing inscriptions in the forgotten language Affa.

It had rich deposits of gemstones and precious metals, spices, and valuable hardwoods which grew in abundance. The presence of these raw materials combined with its advantageous position en route to Zakhara's trading partners in the far east made Afyal one of the wealthiest areas of the continent. Fabulous jewelry was one of their prime exports.

entities.name: Agate Anchor
entities.description:
The Agate Anchor was a curio shop in the city of Tantras in the Vast around 1358 DR.

The shop lay on Dragonleather Street, in the southern part of the city.

The Agate Anchor was a vast curio shop that apparently stocked every non-magical item around.

Chuldos was the proprietor of the Agate Anchor, and Alaphale and Nuathue were guards.
entities.short_description: The Agate Anchor was a curio shop in the city of Tantras in the Vast around 1358 DR.

entities.name: Agatha's Grove
entities.description:
Agatha's Grove was the lair of the banshee Agatha, the "Ghost of Neverwinter Wood".

The grove was northwest of the Conyberry area at the end of a path whose entrance was marked by a group of birch trees in the Neverwinter Wood in northwest Faerûn.

The banshee's home was constructed out of a dome of branches with a single hole for an entrance, where individuals had to get on hands and feet to crawl through the opening. Once inside the structure, Agatha placed a mirror on the far wall to help create illusions of herself. The final room in her tree cave was the treasure room.

Agatha's lair used to be guarded by a magic mirror spell, which hid her exact location for intruders and give her time to hurl spells. After the robbery of her mask, Agatha built new defenses around her home. Her spells enabled her to charm owlbears and she convinced the villagers of Conyberry to dig pitfall traps around her grove. These townsfolk had also been seen guarding her lair. In addition, Agatha wedged wands into trees throughout her haunt and aimed them toward the path to her grove.
entities.short_description: Agatha's Grove was the lair of the banshee Agatha, the "Ghost of Neverwinter Wood".

entities.name: Agathea's hut
entities.description:
Agathea's hut was a hut in the Underdark near the drow city of Sschindylryn—the home of the night hag Agathea.

The hut was built into the end of a cavern, and was peculiarly built in the manner of a wooden house with a thatched roof, resembling a surface structure. The interior was warm and cozy, with a large cage for keeping guests in, and a large kitchen and dining table for serving them.

The hut was near to Nessaleesa's Garden and the Great Waterfall. The tunnel to the hut was lined with large traps that caught travelers, right up to the front door.

entities.name: Agathys
entities.description:
Unlike other layers of Carceri, Agathys consisted of a single orb. It was one covered in black ice with red streaks in it.

Apart from the dangers of a minor negative-dominant layer, Agathys was dangerously cold for unprotected people.

The air was quite thin and made it hard for people to exert themselves. Staying in one place was dangerous for anybody. People could become embedded in the ice through freezing.

Petitioners of Agathys were the souls of false friends and those who betrayed trust. They had to constantly move, lest they be captured in the ice. Agathys was full of frozen bodies and while they could not talk, because their lips were frozen shut, they screamed when the ice moved and crushed them. If they were helped, for which they promised anything, they betrayed their saviors at their first chance to do so.
entities.short_description: Unlike other layers of Carceri, Agathys consisted of a single orb. It was one covered in black ice with red streaks in it.

entities.name: Ageadren
entities.description:
Ageadren was one of the Six Holy Cities of the ixitxachitl nation in the Sea of Fallen Stars known as the Xedran Reefs.

Like all of the 'chitl cities, Orilidren consisted of a huge warren of tunnels and subcaverns. This included a central entrance to the surface, with passages riddled in traps, and large cavern beneath that site with a great temple to Ilxendren around which the rest of the city grew outward from.

There stood an outbuilding near the temple for the Devitan's personal slaves, at least four caverns on the outskirts of the city in which other slaves were kept, two military garrisons, and at least four public shrines on the city outskirts that were deciated to Ilxendren.

Around the 3 to 9 day of Lifesong, These forces would go on to destroy the two cities' supporting temples at Ilramas, Ilkanar, Ilphaeth, and Ilteon were destroyed.

entities.name: Agenais
entities.description:
Agenais was a tiny empire of the Whamite Isles in the Sea of Fallen Stars. It participated in a series of wild conflicts against the other nations and pirates of the Whamite Isles

Agenais was on the southernmost island of the Whamite Islands. It shared major land borders with the Land of the Beastly Brigands and Wolfenbutte, and a minor one with Swil. A distinctive mountain range marked Agenais's border with the Land of the Beastly Brigands and along its coastline that overlooked the Swil Passage.

Perhaps the only settlement on Agenais was a small village by the side of a hill. It had a white lighthouse and a dock. The other buildings there were divided between common and more wealthy sections. The streets were narrow and cobbled. In the water, there was a circle of standing stones sacred to Eldath. The stones were made from white marble and coral.

When the kelpie summoned by Iakhovas as part of the Twelfth Serôs War compelled the people of the Whamites to drown themselves en masse, Agenais was desolated. In mid-Mirtul of the , an adventuring party sent by Andeth Ilchammar to establish diplomatic relations with Myth Nantar arrived in Agenais. They were sent there through a portal at the request of the Nantarn Council, who demanded that they return the Crown of Salt from Agenais. After avoiding the song of the kelpie, and the undead that prowled Agenais, they came to the lighthouse. There, they faced off against Vilander and his traps to recover the crown from him.

entities.name: Agis
entities.description:
Agis was an ancient town of the Calimshan Empire and later the Port Town of Shoonach. It shared the name with Fort Agis and the River Agis upon which they sat.

Agis was the southernmost urban area of Shoonach, and sat upon a small peninsula on the River Agis below the Palace Mount. In the west it connected to the wide-spreading Fedhiyajar farmlands, and was close to the Mamlukkar and Imperial City. A long bridge crossed the water from Agis, reaching the eastern end of the Imperial City.

The town was predominantly made up of docks and warehouses, the rotting remains of which endured to later ages. A wall stretched across the neck of the peninsula, separating it from the Fedhiyajar. Like other parts of Shoonach, ancient water pumps from the time of Shanatar remained intact and functional, providing clean water to the area's fountains.

Agis was present as a river port in , when the construction efforts of Shoonach began upon the nearby hill, creating the Imperial City and Palace Mount. Agis became the dedicated port for the entire urban complex that sprung forth, carrying traffic to and from the River Agis.

entities.name: River Agis
entities.description:
The River Agis flowed from the east out of the Marching Mountains and into the Trackless Sea near the city of Memnon.

It served as the border between Calimshan and Tethyr ever since the Eye Tyrant Wars.

The river was wide and slow-moving and very suitable for cargo-carrying barges and lumber.

The river became the border between Tethyr and Calimshan in the , when the syl-pasha of Calimport, Kamus el Tarshaj, ceded the lands of Monrativi Teshy Mir over to Tethyr—supposedly as a reward for Tethyr's assistance in the Eye Tyrant Wars more than a decade earlier.

entities.name: Aglarond
entities.description:
Aglarond (}}) was a magocratic state in the southwestern-most part of the Unapproachable East with its capital at Veltalar. Most of its land was covered by the Yuirwood. Filled with magic and mystery, it was ruled by one of the most potent spellcasters of the Realms: the Simbul, until , and around 1479 DR, it was ruled by fifteen Simbarchs, arcane spellcasters trained in the Simbul's arts.

There was only one major port in Aglarond, Velprintalar, later known as Veltalar. The large peninsula's coastline mainly comprised rocky cliffs with villages and towns settled near inlets suitable only for fishing boats and other smaller ships.

As of 1479 DR, the Yuirwood was filled with plaguelands formed in the wake of the Spellplague, filled with ruins of an ancient, long-gone eladrin civilization.

The larger cities in Aglarond were the coastal ones. Most cities were supported by agriculture or fishing. Wealthier inhabitants lived in stone buildings, the poor lived in thatched huts, and those in-between lived in buildings of two or three stories, made of weathered wood with steep shale or tile roofs. Construction was usually dense, with narrow streets.

entities.name: Agmoth Road
entities.description:
Agmoth Road was a short road that connected the small town of Moranay with the Royal Road of Impiltur that spanned the length of the Easting Coast.

Traffic along the road was not very busy. However the road was used to convey shipments of gold and silver ore, from the mines of the Earthfast Mountains to the royal mint in the city of Hlammach.

entities.name: Agri Plantation
entities.description:
Agri Plantation was the biggest plantation in northern Thay.

Around 1352 DR, Blackland's son Wynter left the plantation his father worked at and left Thay, eventually becoming a Harper.

By 1362 DR Blackland Ironhoof had been running the plantation for some time, making almost all of his slave purchasing in Eltabbar, while the Agri Plantation had a good slave breeding program in place.

entities.name: Agricultural Promenade
entities.description:
The Agricultural Promenade, or Farmers' Road, was located in Huzuz, the City of Delights, in 1367 DR.

The Farmers' Road separated the Clothiers' District and Peasants' District, branching off from the Road to Enlightenment near the Gulf Gate to run north roughly parallel to Clothiers' Way before terminating at the Grand Bazaar in the Merchants' District.

entities.description:
Agundar Villa was the family estate of the Waterdhavian noble house Agundar.

The Agundar Villa was situated on the corner of Copper Street and Hassantyr's Street, in the North Ward of Waterdeep.

This building complex consisted of two high quality buildings, one that was three stories tall and another that stood a single story tall,

entities.name: Ahghairon's Tower
entities.description:
Ahghairon's Tower was the home and eventually the final resting place of Ahghairon, the first Open Lord of Waterdeep.

Ahghairon's Tower was located in a courtyard at the intersection of the Street of Silks and Waterdeep Way in the Castle Ward of Waterdeep.

Ahghairon's Tower was haunted by several grim sights. One was the skeleton of Melkar of Mirabar, a wizard who had attempted to breach the tower. His skeleton stood inside the magical fields facing the north side of the tower, with its arms stretched wide.

Local children made it a game to rearrange the bones inside the fields with a long stick, as the bones would always eventually drift back into position. The practice was eventually banned by the Open Lord, Piergeiron Paladinson.

entities.name: Ahlarkhem
entities.description:
Ahlarkhem was a barony of Erlkazar encompassing the High Peaks and their evirons.

Ahlarkhem Barony was the center of trade for the kingdom of Erlkazar. The barony contained nine villages, which thrived on farming, fishing, and mining. The troops here also were responsible for defending the country from the goblins of the Cloven Mountains.

Ahlarkhem was the southeastern barony, neighbored by Tanistan to the west and Shalanar to the northwest. Shalane Lake and the Deepwash formed its northern border, and the High Peaks of the Cloven Mountains took up most of its southern territory.

Flowing through the High Peaks toward the Deepwash, the Arglander River was located in this region. It only had a single crossing, the Shadebridge on the road from Duhlnarim to Saarlik. The Wintercloak River also ran through this barony.

entities.name: Ahlmer's General Store
entities.description:
Ahlmer's General Store was a shop in the city of Procampur in the Vast in the late 14 century DR. It was owned and run by Ahlmer.

The prices were low and among its goods were fresh-baked biscuits for which the store was famed.

In Alturiak in the , a strange well-dressed gentleman found wandering the streets of Procampur identified himself as "Lord Sellwin Wagglebottom, Deputy Assistant Commander in charge of Perishable Supply Requisition for the Armies of Ravens Bluff" and asked for directions to Ahlmer's General Store.

entities.name: Ahoyhoy
entities.description:
Ahoyhoy was a fort on the northwest coast of the Snout of Omgar. It was inhabited by tortles.

Ahoyhoy was built with large stone walls―adorned with massive tortoise shells―that formed a multi-tiered stronghold.

The fort was located at the top of a rocky shelf, overlooking a beach. Numerous shipwrecks were strewn across the shore north of the village.

A lone trail connected Ahoyhoy to the Typhoon Palace of Dangwaru.

entities.name: Ahruukar
entities.description:
Ahruukar () was a small realm of gold dwarves in east Faerûn. It was home to the Ruuk clan of dwarves.

The realm lay deep below the Thesk Mountains, near Thesk.

The dwarves of Ruuk lacked the arrogance that was often seen in gold dwarves, and were quite cosmopolitan and worldly. They had a strategic and philosophical attitude with the wider world, and sought to manipulate the Realms into engaging in energetic trading and prosperity, and avoiding raiding and war. Despite this pacifistic and intellectual bent, the dwarves were fearless in battle even against dragons.

As of the 15 century DR, the realm mined and worked iron and hematite from the mountains, as well as great riches of sapphires, citrines, peridots, and spinels. They traded with the wider world at Phsant.
entities.short_description: Ahruukar () was a small realm of gold dwarves in east Faerûn. It was home to the Ruuk clan of dwarves.

entities.name: Ahs Trango Shan
entities.description:
Ahs Trango Shan, or the South Guardian Peak, was a mountain located in Khazari.

The South Guardian Peak formed part of the natural border of eastern Khazari, along with the Nas Trango Shan, providing a rocky barrier against Kara-Tur and the outside world.

At , the South Guardian Peak was the smaller of two peaks located in eastern Khazari. The Broken Wall Pass ran between the two peaks.

Strong fortifications, in the form of fort Luntse Dzong, were present to ensure the protection of the valuable Silk Road that passed through the mountains.

entities.name: Ahtahqugotak Sea
entities.description:
The Ahtahqugotak Sea was a body of water in Ibelgrak Valley in Angalpuk on the Great Glacier.

The Ahtahqugotak Sea was the largest sea in Angalpuk, at almost across at its widest point, but also quite shallow, being only deep. In winter, it was covered in thick ice, and in spring this broke apart as platform ice. In summer, it was nearly ice-free. Its waters were clear and calm, while it shores were dense with white birches and lush evergreens, making it possibly the most picturesque sea on the Great Glacier.

Its waters were fertile with game fish, such as bloatfish, black burners, and polar cod. The surrounding area was almost free of predators and hunters, so caribou, musk oxen, and many kinds of birds were abundant.

Despite the abundant game animals and fish, many Angulutiuns avoided the Ahtahqugotak, fearing the fever virus that had spread from the Ibelgrak Valley in the Year of Scorching Suns, 460 DR, to kill thousands. However, there was no evidence that the disease lurked in the Ahtahqugotak water or the local wildlife.

entities.name: Ahtitlak
entities.description:
Ahtitlak was a village located in the Alpuk region of the Great Glacier.

Unlike most Ulutiun settlements, the residents of Ahtitlak did not live within minikitaks or snowhouses. In fact, the hardy villagers did not use any sort of structure to sleep in. Instead, they slept in the cavern around a large communal fire, using wolf-skins as bedding.

Ahtitlak was located in the south-eastern corner of Alpuk, entirely within a massive cavern along the western tip of the Lugsaas Chain.

Around 359 DR, the urit of a community in Nakvaligach received a kaiurit. The edict commanded the small village to migrate far to the south, where they were told a physical manifestation of Ulutiu would appear. When they arrived at their destination, they discovered a massive cavern inhabited by remorhazes. Since the villagers had never heard of or seen remorhazes before, they assumed the remorhazes were the physical manifestation of Ulutiu and decided to settle within the cavern.
entities.short_description: Ahtitlak was a village located in the Alpuk region of the Great Glacier.

entities.name: Aib
entities.description:
Aib was a small town found within interior Zakhara.

Aib sat along the western banks of the North Quarter of Suq Bay. It was nestled in the foothills of the eastern end of the Spine of the Dog due south of Hiyal. A pair of intermittent rivers provided Aib with a source of fresh water at different times of the year.

entities.name: Air District
entities.description:
The Air District was a collection of 36 earthmotes that became a prestigious neighborhood of Yhaunn.

When the Spellplague struck in the , the surrounding cliffs and slopes of the city shattered and broke away, falling upwards into the sky along with the wreckage of the upper-class mansions that had been built on them. Nearly ten thousand people died in the event, though the city eventually recovered with the assistance of their Shadovar masters. The earthmotes were eventually inhabited and became the Air District, home of luxurious mansions, with the highest earthmotes having the most prestige.

entities.name: Airspur
entities.description:
Airspur was a powerful trading port city in western Chessenta in the Old Empires. It was a highly cosmopolitan and multiracial city, with an impressively high population of orcs and half-orcs. The genasi would call the old city Ancient Airspur.

Airspur stood in the north-west corner of Chessenta, on the southwestern shore of the Wizards' Reach and with the Akanapeaks in the west. A trail ran west through the mountains to Reth and another ran southeast along the coast to Cimbar.

Formerly a possession of the empire of Unther, the cities of Chessenta rebelled and formed the Alliance of Chessenta under the leadership of the warlord Tchazzar of Cimbar. Driving Untheric forces from the land, they seceded from Unther in the Year of Flashing Eyes, 929 DR. Thereafter, they stood as a part of the Union of Chessenta, a confederation of city-states that swelled into the Chessentan Empire ruled by Tchazzar. However, with Tchazzar's death or disappearance in the Year of the Dracorage, 1018 DR, the Empire broke apart and declined. Although each city-state had sworn fealty to a central monarch, after Tchazzar, they disagreed on who this should be. Finally, in the Year of the Twelverule, 1117 DR, the realm broke up into a number of feuding city-states, with an ever-changing network of alliances, conflicts, and factions.

In the centuries between the break-up and the early 14 century, Airspur and Cimbar fought two wars.

At its southern end, the street approached Aithe Keep as it left town. This section of the street was known as the Foregate.

entities.name: Ajayib
entities.description:
Ajayib, also called the "City of Wonders", was the youngest of Zakhara's Pearl Cities, and its most westerly. Beyond it lay the wilderness of al-Suqut Mountains.

Located along the western coast of the Crowded Sea along the banks of Al-Malja River, Ajayib was both the southernmost and westernmost of the major Pearl Cities.

The source of Ajayib's wealth was cultivated on the steep hills which rose above the city. Though famous for their splendid coffee, Ajayib also exported fruits, frankincense, and other aromatic gums. The productions of bright dyes was also a major portion of their trade dealings.

Ajayib was the youngest of the great Pearl Cities, having only established an enlightened mosque in 1357 DR.

entities.name: Ajhuutal
entities.description:
Ajhuutal was a city built by the marid Ajhuu and his followers when they rebelled against the djinni Calim and founded the Maridlands.

The city was built on a coastal promontory west of the Alimir Mountains, in what was then the eastern extent of the Calim Empire. Following its destruction it sat in of water in the Shining Sea, south of Almraiven at the underwater edge of the bay.

When Calim's empire building paused in to appease the Shanatar dwarves and the elves of Tethir and Darthiir, his marid vassal Ajhuu took it as a sign of weakness and seized the eastern frontier of the Calim Empire, founding the Maridlands. The Steam Clashes that followed were highly destructive, culminating in the Shattering in . With a great genie-crafted ritual, Calim created an earthquake that smashed the city and the surrounding area, causing it to fall into the sea. The power of the magic was grossly excessive, however, and it caused thousands of square miles of land to break up, collapse, and be replaced by rushing waters as the coastline was reshaped.

While Ajhuu and his realm was destroyed, the city itself remained mostly intact under more than 300 feet of water. Encrusted with corals and seaweeds, it came to be inhabited by merfolk and some sea elves who took control of the remaining marid magics of the city, creating a mythal-like field over the city that let them control the waters around it. When the Curse of Irphong sank the Pasha's Palace in the , the residents of Ajhuutal and the undersea Dragon's Neck Peninsula thoroughly looted the wreck, carrying off valuable rust-resistant magical tools and weapons while the kraken and sahuagin focused on gold and other treasures.

entities.description:
The Ajmer Forest was located in northeast Durpar in the Shining Lands in 1367 DR.

This tropical rainforest was stiflingly hot and humid.

The Ajmer Forest was home to the only sizable community of elves within Durpar. These elves were unique among their kind in that they followed the teachings of Adama. The elves monitored the loggers to make sure they collected their timber in a manner that would allow the forest to recover quickly.

The southern regions of the forest were home to monsters and many exotic animals. It was even rumored that a rakshasa noble had a headquarters there.

entities.name: Akanal
entities.description:
The Akanal, also known as the Akanul and the Akanul Plains, was a stretch of land in southwestern Chessenta, famed as being among the most fertile farmland anywhere in the Realms.

The Akanal comprised the peninsula between the Akanamere's western and southern arms and the lands around the lake's southern shore. The east and south were bordered by the Hills of Maerth.

Circa 1357 DR, the settlements of the Akanal paid tribute to the city-state of Akanax on a regular basis.

The Akanal boasted incredibly fertile and productive farmland, and was the best in Chessenta and the Old Empires and among the finest in all of Faerûn. The lands around the Akanamere were planted with cash crops in large plantations. Their produce was shipped to Akanax and Soorenar, and from there to Airspur, Cimbar, and Reth, and all in all provided more than half of Chessenta's food supply.

entities.name: Akanamere
entities.description:
The Akanamere was a large freshwater lake,

The Akanamere was a lake rich with fish, while its shores were some of the richest farmlands in Faerûn.

A kingdom of nixies could be found underneath the waters of the Akanamere. The peaceful creatures engaged in trade with the humans of the Blade Kingdoms and were allied with them during the reign of Princess Krrrr-poka. Nixie political dignitaries were guests during the annual celebration of the Festival of Blades. Nixies of Krrrr-poka's kingdom aided fishing city-states of Zutria and Lomatra by driving schools of fish into fishing nets and guarding them against hungry pikes, common within the lake. Nixies received dried beef and squeeze bulbs filled with wine in exchange.

The Akanamere produced a rich catch of fish to the cities on its shores and the nixie population that dwelt in its waters. Eels, stone crabs, and druth were the most common catch. Fresh fish was often sun-dried for storage or trade, and crab was stored in salt-filled barrels. Dried fish was often used in stews and soups, shredded, and cooked in water. The Akanamere's eels were known for their nutty flavor, while flatfish had a distinct smoky taste that resembled pig bacon. Among other fish that was fished from the lake and traded by nixies were blowfish, hogfish, and singing fish.

entities.name: Akanapeaks
entities.description:
The Akanapeaks were a mountain range in Chessenta, forming its historical western border. The south-western part of the Akanapeaks was claimed by the Blade Kingdoms.

The range ran south by the western side of the Akanamere.

The south-western part of the Akanapeaks housed the city-states of Kirenzia, Sumbria, and Zutria that were nestled between the Akanamere and the Akanapeaks. The city-state of Colletro stood within the south-western part of the Akanapeaks, in the rich Valley of Umbricci, with a single mountain pass that led to the Trevi River and joined the rest of the Blade Kingdoms on the lake's shores.

Iron was mined in the safer parts of the Akanapeaks, and this supplied the nearby city of Reth and other parts of Chessenta in mid–14 century DR.

entities.name: Akanax
entities.description:
Akanax was a harsh, warlike city in the Akanal region of Chessenta known for its talented smiths, its rigid military structure, and its intolerance of outsiders. It collected tithes and tributes from the Akanal region and conquered settlements such as Rodanar and Oslin

Structures within Akanax typically lacked ornamentation, and the majority of its population lived in tents surrounding the city.

By 1357 DR, Akanax had an army of 15,000 infantry units and 5,000 archers. It also controlled 10 warships.

Criminal matters in Akanax were decided primarily by a military tribune, but the king also possessed the power to exile or execute any dissent to his rule.

entities.name: Akano River
entities.description:
The Akano River was a river on the eastern side of the main island of Tsukishima in Wa.

The river was located north of the city of Uwaji. The tributaries of the river flowed down from the Ikuyu Mountains. The river flowed north parallel to Tawata Road and the coast, past Rukimbaru, and then turned east to empty into the sea near the town of Chozawa.

Chozawa Castle was located on the high ground above the river.

In the first year of the reign of Kochi, Master of the Peach Tree, the first emperor of Wa, the first ever ch'i-lin rose from the waters of the Akano River and presented itself to Kochi. Upon the ch'i-lin's back were a series of characters, from which Kochi created the first written form of the Wa-an language.

entities.name: Akanûl
entities.description:
Akanûl was a land that once belonged to the world of Abeir as part of the realm of Shyr, but was transposed onto the plane of Toril during the ravages of the Spellplague. The land carried with it a large population of Abeiran genasi who, as of 1479 DR, controlled the region that used to be Chondath and western Chessenta.

Akanûl resembled Abeir much more than Toril. The vast majority of land was a hodgepodge of spectacular spires and erratic ravines. It boasted the largest number of earthmotes and watermotes in all of Faerûn. The southern edge of the region was bordered by a large finger of the Underchasm. One of the land's more unusual features was an enormous piece of translucent quartz known as the Glass Mesa, which citizens were forbidden to approach.

Akanûl was primarily temperate, but, owing to the large amount of wild elemental energy lingering from the separation from Abeir, wind patterns were erratic, as was weather. The climate in Akanûl was largely humid, because of the constant drift of mist and rain from the watermotes that floated over the countryside.

As a genasi-dominated nation, Akanûl's social structure, while largely authoritarian, was highly meritocratic in nature and most genasi could aspire to great heights if they were talented and worked hard enough. Circa 1479 DR, the ruler of the kingdom was Queen Arathane, who ruled from an enormous floating spire. Queen Arathane played a large part in Akanûl's society and was responsible for the ultimate well-being of her citizens, which she took very seriously.

entities.name: Al-Akara Mountains
entities.description:
Al-Akara Mountains, also called the Mountains of Creation, were a prominent mountain range found in the heart of interior Zakhara.

The mountain range ran for hundreds of miles roughly west to east, abutting the fertile Al-Sarif River valley near Huzuz in the west and passing southeast into the Cities of the Pantheon, effectively creating a border from the Cities of the Heart. A long arm of the mountains sprouted from its center, reaching north into the barren Genies' Anvil of the Haunted Lands.

entities.description:
Akarav's Bay was the northernmost bay of Lake Esmel in Amn.

The bay contained Lake Esmel's largest concentration of mineral springs, which kept the waters warm and provided health benefits to those bathing within.

In addition to many springs, Akarav's Bay was fed by the Splendarrllur.

The bay was named after a priest of Waukeen who discovered the springs and founded the first resort to take advantage of the waters,

entities.description:
Akari was the largest of the Prioto Islands, a small group of islands in the Yellow Sea south of Kozakura.

They were resettled by Shou Lung in 1357 DR. Akari was the site of the main Shou colony.

entities.name: Akashnu Mountains
entities.description:
The Akashnu Mountains stood in the land of Malatra in Kara-Tur and were the birthplace of the Kuong Kingdom.

The mountains towered 6000–7000 feet (1.8–2.1 kilometers) over the jungles of Malatra. They had very rough terrain and rocky peaks, with a number of valleys between the ridges.

The range was rich in gems and precious metals.

The Akashnu Mountains were where the Kuong Kingdom arose, founded by Vishnan I with its priest-kings ruling from the capital city of Suranatra. From the outset, it was an aggressive and theocratic empire. Thanks to the precious metals and stones found in the Akashnu Mountains, the rich and puissant priest-kings of Suranatra expanded their dominion to the Kunong River and to the coast.

entities.name: Lake Akax
entities.description:
Lake Akax, also known as the Ghostmere, was a lake found in the borderlands between Akanûl and Chessenta during the 15 century DR.

Lake Akax was a deep, hypersaline lake, and its waters were home to strange elemental oozes that could mimic the forms of those who drowned in the lake. For this reason the lake was feared by most people. During winters, the borders of Lake Akax became a solidified, caustic sludge that could dissolve flesh and bone.

The lake had a long and misshapen form that stretched from the dry interior uplands of western Chessenta and Akanûl down to the former mouth of the Akax River at the ruins of Soorenar. The River Akax continued to flow down from the lake across the expansive Adder Swamp until it flowed into the diminished Bay of Chessenta. The settlements of Thurik and Jeblant were found on its northern shores, while the south and east merged into the Adder Swamp.

The lake was formed from the remnants of the River Akax and the Akanamere, which were heavily altered by the ravages of the Spellplague in 1385 DR. While the Akanamere shrank to Stoneshield Lake and Lake Fand and its flow redirected into the Adder River via the Belur River, the River Akax was cut off and largely swallowed by the vastly expanded Adder Swamp, forming Lake Akax.

entities.description:
The River Akax was a river located in the country of Chessenta.

The river flowed from the Akanamere in the southwest to empty into the western coast of the Bay of Chessenta. The river split the city of Soorenar into eastern and western halves.

The entire length of the River Akax was navigable by small and medium-sized vessels.

entities.name: Akhir
entities.description:
Akhir was a ruined city which was taken into a subdimensional bubble by Martek to serve as a test within his tomb after its inhabitants had all died. The Lancers of Death began every nightly assault on the Crypt of Al-Alisk from the city's ruins.

Sometime during the mid-to-late 3 century DR, the Princess of Pazar, Sithal Al-Husn, was bethrothed to Athis Al-Din of Akhir. The princess was kidnapped on her wedding night by Habrauk Al-Nirin of the Al-Alisk clan; this started a blood feud which, together with the drying of the River Athis due to the Curse of Amun-Re, ended the bloodlines of Pazar, Akhir, and the Al-Alisk clan within five generations.

After the end of their bloodlines, however, Akhir and the Crypt of Al-Alisk became the site of a nightly battle in which the Lancers of Death, the restless spirits of the warriors from Pazar and Akhir that perished in the conflict, emerged from the ruined city to strike at the crypt; there, they were met by the spirits of the fallen from the Al-Alisk clan.

Martek stole away the depopulated ruin to serve as a test sometime around the year . In the year , adventurers released Princess Sithal Al-Husn, thus releasing all of the undead from their nightly combat.

entities.name: Akhlaur Swamp
entities.description:
The swamp covered, as of 1373 DR, an oblong area roughly 4000 square miles (6437.3 sq km.). The Swamp of Akhlaur was filled with cypress trees, moss and assortment of fauna including crocodiles and dangerous piranha. Unnatural creatures such as undead were also present.

Laraken also inhabited the swamp, making this a dangerous location for any spellcaster.

The swamp was named for the famed conjurer Akhlaur. It was believed he perished here when he was taken to the Elemental Plane of Water by a summoned laraken. The portal through which he disappeared remained open, allowing a constant flow of water to expand the swamp at a rate of an additional 100 ft. (30 m) per year. Akhlaur's Tower remained long after his passing.

In 1373 DR, the magehound Kiva managed to remove the portal from the swamp, successfully halting its advance.

entities.name: Akhlaur's Tower
entities.description:
Akhlaur's tower was created by the eponymous wizard in 12th-century DR.

The tower resided in the middle of the swamp that bore the spellcaster's name and had long since been abandoned since he called it home. As the waters of the swamp grew, the tower sunk, and became partially submerged. In the Year of Wild Magic the tower stood out enough to still be entered and explored.

Considering how powerful a wizard Akhlaur was, there was likely a wealth of magical items and arcane secrets inside.

entities.name: Aki's
entities.description:
Aki's was a well-known restaurant in the town of Aru in Wa in the 1770s on the Wa Calendar. It was run by Aki Marushima. It stood in the Mixed District, beside the gate to the Merchant District and directly opposite rival restaurant Tojo's.

In , Aki declared his restaurant to be the best in Aru, but so did his brother and business rival Tojo. To settle the question, they each might've offered a group of adventurers a free meal, one night after the other, so they could serve as impartial judges. However, Tojo would pay a person to slip a mild purgative into their food when they dined at Aki's, which would cause them gastrointestinal problems during their adventures.

entities.name: Akintaer
entities.description:
Akintaer, also known as Quagmire, was a floating Netherese enclave known for its worship of Targus, and for the strength of its army.

The enclave was located above the Watercourse river, at the south end of the Marsh of Simplicity, which in turn lay south of the Narrow Sea.

Owing perhaps to its swampy surroundings, Akintaer seemed perpetually rain-slick and covered in mildew and moss.

Akintaer was founded in by a mysterious archwizard. The only characteristic known about this figure is his unwavering devotion to the bloody war god Targus, and his insistence that all within his enclave commit themselves to this religion. The archwizard was highly focused on martial prowess, and fostered the art of warfare in his enclave's enormous Temple of Targus. As a result, Akintaer's army was prized both for its strength of numbers, but also for the skill and ferocity of its soldiers, unrivaled in all of Netheril. Other Netherese cities were happy to send their warriors to Akintaer to learn and benefit from the enclave's expertise.

entities.name: Mount Akka
entities.description:
Mount Akka was a mountain in the Alpuk region of the Great Glacier.

Mount Akka was a tall mountain, up to in elevation, with a double peak. It was located in the southern edge of the Surykyk Range. Within the mountain is a network of interconnected caverns.

Mount Akka was a popular nesting grounds for wild kupuk. Kupuk made nests and laid their eggs with the caves under the mountain. The caves provided shelter from the weather and protection from predators.

entities.name: Akkaido
entities.description:
Akkaido was a major port city of the island of Tsukishima, Wa, that catered to both sea-faring

The city's most prominent feature was its harbors that held several hundred vessels, both fishing and mercantile.

Akkaido was built on the hilly southern shores of Tsukishima. The lands that became Akkaido were known for being natural harbors of the Sea of Patience.

In 1754, the nation of Wa was forced to cut most of its international trade under the rulership of Shogun Matasuuri Nagahide. Despite its centuries-long international trade, Akkaido became the only trade port of Wa open to foreign merchants. All international imports were strictly regulated and placed under imposed limits. Despite that, the city's busy trade brought dozens of ships filled with exotic goods on a daily basis. The main consumers of expensive imported goods were upper-class inhabitants of Wa.

entities.name: Akota
entities.description:
Akota was a mysterious country somewhere beyond the western shores of Zakhara.

Akota exported gold, slaves, wood, and exotic goods to the Land of Fate through the city of Akota to the city of Tajar.

It had its own language called Akotan, which was also spoken in Zakhara's western settlements that were conducting trade with exotic Akota.

The Scholar's View of Toril map from the Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition and the Forgotten Realms Interactive Atlas show a number of islands of greatly varying size to the west of Zakhara. Some or all of them may represent the country of Akota. Otherwise, Akota may lie on the continents of Katashaka or Arandron.

entities.description:
Akpahlurik Lake was a lake in the Alpuk region of the Great Glacier.

Akpahlurik Lake was a salt water lake with an average depth of between . Along the southern shore, oil desposits oozed from the lake bed. The oil was skimmed and collected from the water.

Akpahlurik Lake was located in eastern Alpuk, between the Lugalpgotak Sea and the Keryjek Ridge.

The turbulent Akundi River was located in Ra-Khati.

The Akundi River connected the lake of Manasowar with another unnamed lake high in the Katakoro Shan mountain range.

entities.name: Al Qahara
entities.description:
Al Qahara was a hidden elven town located in a cavern in the southern Raurin desert. The settlement was isolated but did some trade with oasis settlements in the desert.

The entrance to the town was located in the face of a ravine; inside the mouth, there was a lantern-lit cavern with a gate. Beyond the gate was a large plaza lit by oil lamps, with a mosaic covering the floor, where the walls were covered with bronze calligraphic plaques and tapestries. This was the common area of Al Qahara. Around its walls were a number of balconies, square tunnels, and galleries. The mosaic hid a high-walled well at the center of the plaza.

The cave mouth was hidden with enchantments of misdirection. Five guards kept watch over the gate, and they could call on reinforcements

In the , Kiril Duskmourn visited Al Qahara, looking for shelter from a coming storm, and a healer's attention for her companion in the trip, the dwarf geomancer Thormud Horn.

entities.name: Al-Anwahr
entities.description:
Al-Anwahr was an ancient ruin found along the northern reaches of the Haunted Lands in a region known as the Burning Lands in Zakhara in 1367 DR.

Al-Anwahr was found wedged between the blistering Great Anvil and the Sea of Salt.

Al-Anwahr was a powerful city-state during the 5 century DR. At that time the lands surrounding the city were quite fertile, allowing the city to flourish in the surrounding harsh environment of interior Zakhara.

Azaltin ibn Issad was the ruler of the city during this time of prosperity. Much of Al-Anwahr was destroyed during a civil war between Azaltin and his brother, Amakim.

entities.name: Al-Azid's Ghostly Palace
entities.description:
Al-Azid's Ghostly Palace was a magical building connected to a cursed key to its front gate, which could summon the palace to wherever the wielder desired.

The palace typically resided on the Ethereal plane, but could be summoned by the wielder of its gate key to appear in any plane in the multiverse.

This huge palace was made from fine white marble and was decorated with slender minarets, topped with gleaming golden ornaments.

The palace was invisible during the day, though occupants could see everything within the palace once they were inside. At night the palace shone with a white light. The palace was also protected against scrying.

entities.name: Al-Ubaid
entities.description:
The Walled City of Al-Ubaid was a tiny city-state of the Whamite Isles in the Sea of Fallen Stars. It participated in a series of wild conflicts against the other nations and pirates of the Whamite Isles

Al-Ubaid had a variety of colorful political figures that vied for control of the nation and the Whamite Isles. Known individuals were Anndoquat the Sardar, Felquish the Merchant, Dandarnab the Trader, and Count Clannano. It was served by twin legions: the Kardic Legion and the Neddic Legion. Anndoquat also kept a private bodyguard force. The common people of Al-Ubaid, loyal to their home, also joined in the wars of the Whamite isles.

Al-Ubaid was located in the mountain range that formed the border between Klocckbarn and Zagrus. Although smaller than its neighbors, it boasted impressive fortifications like the Gate of Odendog and the South Citadel.

Among the nations of the Whamites, Al-Ubaid was the only known city-state.

entities.name: Alabaster Stonecrafts
entities.description:
Alabaster Stonecrafts was a stonemason's workshop in the Tumbledown neighborhood of Baldur's Gate's Outer City in the late 15 century DR.

Alabaster Stonecrafts was an open-air workshop with tarps stretched overhead to offer some protection from the elements. The workshop's name was stamped on the tarp, announcing itself to passebys.

The workshop was run by dwarf twins who went by "Sister Alabaster" and "Brother Alabaster." The twins happily whistled as they chiselled at the stone. They enjoyed sniping teasing remarks at each other. On Kythorn 28 of the , Alabaster Stonecrafts was visited by Tav, an adventuring detective who was investigating a series of grizzly murders. One of the dead bodies was fished out of the River Chionthar, wrapped in a tarp taken from one of the workshops on Misty Court. Tav found the open-air stonemason's workshop, and the twins told the investigator of strange happenings that had been plaguing the nearby Cliffside Cemetery, claiming that the gravedigger – Grom Skullsmash, was responsible for the. Or it were the ghosts if Brother Alabaster was to be believed.

entities.description:
Aladiam's Imports was a shop in Tegal's Mark that sold spices and silks imported from Sembia during the mid-14 century DR. The establishment was run by a retired Calishite adventurer named Aladiam. He was a known smuggler and fence

The shop was defended by some sort of invisible guardian. On one occasion it ripped through three Sembians who confronted Aladiam about some stolen goods.

entities.name: Alagh Rorncaurak
entities.description:
Alagh Rorncaurak, or the Battlecavern of Unquenched Valor, was both a chasm and a temple of Clangeddin Silverbeard, the Father of Battle, in the dwarven city of Earthfast, deep below the Earthfast Mountains between the Vast and Impiltur, in the Earthroot region of the Underdark.

Alagh Rorncaurak was a huge natural chasm that served as a natural cathedral to Clangeddin. It lay in the heart of Earthfast, but with much of the city abandoned, it came to sit on the western edge of the dwarf-held territory.

In the 1360s DR, Alagh Rorncaurak stood on the frontlines of the orcish siege of Earthfast. The orcs launched wave after wave of attacks against it, particularly through the ruined western barracks of the temple.

The immigrating dwarves of Clan Hammerhand were much-needed reinforcements, and their assistance gave the dwarves time to fortify the temple's defences. They kept the temple's central sanctuary and the entrance to the rest of the city free of orcish incursion. But circa 1369 DR, clashes between dwarven defenders and orc patrols remained frequent.

entities.name: Alagh's Pass
entities.description:
Alagh's Pass was a naturally-occurring mountain pass that wound its way through an area of the Sword in the Anauroch desert.

It was regularly intersected by chasms and canyons, that were split by additional crevices.

The pass was located between the a range of mountains in the Saiyaddar and the Hills of Scent.

Alagh's pass featured a single lake that had long since been nearly entirely dried up. All that remained as of the mid−14 century DR was a small muddy pool.
entities.short_description: Alagh's Pass was a naturally-occurring mountain pass that wound its way through an area of the Sword in the Anauroch desert.

entities.name: Alaghôn
entities.description:
Alaghôn, the capital of Turmish, was an ancient city that saw its share of trials and tribulations over the years, ranging from terrible fires to occupation by the blue dragon Anaglathos during the Reign of the Wyrm. Throughout all of this, Alaghôn survived as a trade center known as the "throne of Turmish."

The ancient port city channeled nearly all the trade that Turmish had with the rest of Faerûn for centuries, It was the most popular port on the southern fringes of the Inner Sea.

There were numerous stonemasons involved in the creation of the stone buildings, vaults, houses, and drains that comprised Alaghôn. This construction created "a thousand thousand" hiding places. This fact was especially true where the works of a human stonemason covered up the older workings of a dwarven craftsman. The secret passages and cubby holes created by such overlapping workmanship were popular places for children to play. Sometimes, the children ran into monsters - never again to run through the city streets of Alaghôn. When a child went missing, adventuring companies are sent to investigate.

Alaghôn was divided up into city districts.

entities.name: Alamaqu
entities.description:
Alamaqu was a tent city in the Plain of Horses of northwestern Kara-Tur. It was the home of the T'aghur tribe.

Situated in the central Chigidi Mountains, the city lay in a valley surrounded by high peaks that formed a defensive barrier.

Alamaqu was actually little more than a vast campsite containing thousands of tents, collectively as big and as populous as an average city elsewhere. These tents were the distinctive white ger favored by the T'aghurs, arrayed in long lines along paths wide enough ox- and horse-drawn carts. Each was erected over a shallow pit dug into the earth. In the winter, the T'aghurs packed up their tents and drove their sheep herds to greener fields, leaving Alamaqu nearly empty.

As well as the mountains themselves, Alamaqu was protected by a stone wall some high. While the T'aghurs were away in winter, a small garrison remained behind to watch over the campsite.

entities.name: Alamather's by the Water
entities.description:
Almather's by the Water was a shop in Berdusk in the Western Heartlands in the mid-to-late 14 century DR that specialized in selling rare or unique weapons that were better suited for showmanship or worship than for actual battle.

The small shop sits on the Gollahaer, the shorter street that crossed the Clearspring. It was fairly close to the bookstore Ondraer's Fine Pages.

Almather's by the Water specialized in one-of-a-kind, rare, or unusual weaponry. Examples included cane-swords, gauntlets fitted with hidden dagger blades in the fingers, and barbed-wire whips. The shop also carried a wide array of trapped items, many set up to deliver lethal doses of poison, but the shop could not provide poisons by itself since the sale of venoms and toxins was banned within Berdusk.

Because of the nature of the store's wares, it was frequented by caravan merchants and professional killers.

entities.name: Alamber Sea
entities.description:
The Alamber Sea, also known as the Sahuagin Sea, was the primary trade avenue between the nations of Mulhorand, Unther, Thay, and Tymanther (and for a time, High Imaskar as well). As a result, its waters were considered neutral territory.

As of 1489 DR, the waters of the Alamber Sea were bordered by Mulhorand to the east and Unther and Tymanther to the west. The nation of Thay bordered the Alamber to the north, except where it connected to the larger Inner Sea. The northernmost island of Alaor served as the center of Thayvian naval power in the region.

Circa 1270 DR, in an elaborate ritual to summon Kossuth's avatar, the high priest of the Kossuthan temple Flaming Brazier in Bezantur attempted to douse the Alamber Sea with a decanter of endless lamp oil and then ignite it. This adversely affected sea life in the Alamber for years to come and engendered hatred in its sahuagin inhabitants towards the port city.

Despite its status as neutral territory, merchant vessels and other ships found in the Alamber Sea were usually Thayvian in origin. A considerable number of pirates frequented these waters, and below the surface lay the sahuagin kingdom of Aleaxtis.

entities.name: River Alamber
entities.description:
The River Alamber was a long and swift river found in the Greenfields in southern Unther and, after the Spellplague, in central Tymanther.

The River Alamber was formed by a network of streams on the northern Unthangol Mountains that flowed east across the Greenfields before draining into the Alamber Sea. Its waters provided sediment for the fertile lands of the Greenfields, but the river was unpredictable in its floods, much like the River Angol.

At least twice in recorded history, in 108 DR and in 731 DR, the city of Unthalass was flooded by the waters of the River Alamber.

During the Spellplague, because of the violent exchange of lands between the worlds of Abeir and Toril, the River Alamber got divided into two sections because of the creation of the Ash Lake. Another lake, Lance Lake, was also created during this cataclysm near the origin of the river, in the Unthangol Mountains.

entities.name: Alamontyr
entities.description:
Alamontyr was a large fishing and agricultural town in the far northeast of the Border Kingdoms. It was the easternmost notable settlement within the Border Kingdoms, and was home to the largest community of craftspeople in the region.

Alamontyr was the first major city encountered by caravans coming down from the Golden Road.

Alamontyr lay on Zarcel's Run, a river that flowed from the Duskwood in the south to the shores of the Lake of Steam in the north.

Alamontyr was ruled by Shield Duke Bardran Thulmaer and his forty Griffon Knights, who policed the town and the surrounding areas fairly and with particular respect for local religious leaders. This made him well-loved not only with the people of Alamontyr but also the people of the Realm of the Smoking Star to the west. The Shield Duke was quite old but had not yet named a successor by 1374 DR, leading to much speculation and meddling.

entities.description:
Alandamer's Gate was the northern gate of the city of Athkatla in Amn.

Alandamer's Gate stood on the border of two districts of Athkatla: the Wave District to the west and the Temple District to the east. The road that passed Alandamer's Gate ran north towards the grand temple complex of the Goldspires and the monastery Arbalest's House.

All non-citizens who passed Alandamer's Gate had to pay an "any one coin" toll, of gold or silver, to be allowed into Athkatla.

entities.description:
The Alandor River was a major river in Amn.

The Alandor was a slow-moving and wide river. Beyond Crimmor, the barges continued east to Lake Weng, but the River Road did not.

The waters of the river were green and had a mild smell.

The river flooded in the early spring. The lands south of the river were good for grazing.

entities.name: Alaor
entities.description:
Alaor, or sometimes the Alaor, was a pair of islands on the Alamber Sea an extension of the eastern Sea of Fallen Stars. For many years it was considered a tharch of Thay and served as a strategical naval stronghold for the magocratic nation.

The crag-covered landscape of Alaor was rough and next to no terrain that was suitable for farming.

Alaor's great harbor was located within an expansive cove that was protected by a natural sea-arch. The islands possessed no other suitable areas where ships could safely dock.

While the island was under Thayan control it maintained the nation's great navy from its vast shipbuilding facilities and military docks. The dozen or so ships, ranging from swift dromonds to great galleys, patrolled the waters of the Alamber Sea and kept them free from savage aquatic creatures and marauding pirates.

entities.name: Alaoreum River
entities.description:
Alaoreum River was a river that began in the Mountains of the Alaoreum, ran south along the shoreline of the Sea of Fallen Stars, and ended in Evenstar Lake.

The flooding of the Alaoreum River became ruinous for the settlement of Morningstar Hollows. It took several seasons for the land to become consumed by swamps and the inhabitants of Morningstar Hollows moved to the nearby town of Velorn's Valor. By the late-14 century DR, the village was believed to be inhabited by a three dozen lizardfolk who claimed the abandoned human lands.

In the , druids of Eldath and the Emerald Enclave clashed with undead armies of mohrg warlord Borran Klosk in service of Malar. The Battle of Morningstar Hollows concluded in the druids rising waters of Alaoreum River, flooding the undead and, eventually, trapped the mohrg beneath Alaghôn.

Borran Klosk was released from his prison in the . Morningstar Hollows were taken by the creature's undead armies once more. Klosk used his necromancy to full his army with long-dead folk, murdered by the Emerald Enclave.
