entities.name: Alaphaer Run
entities.description:
The Alaphaer Run was a fast-flowing, supernaturally cold river that found in the Moonsea North region of North Faerûn.

For much of its length, the river was iced over extensively enough to support a heavily laden sledge, or even a landing dragon.

At least some of its unnatural cold came from blessings bestowed on the waters by the goddess Auril, "Alaphaer" being one of her older names. The river was known to run in and out of Auril's extraplanar Deep Wilds realm several times as it descended from the Mammothbacks of the northern Abbey Mountains and headed for the Frozen Forest.

The river arose and flowed north out of the western Abbey Mountains into the Frozen Forest, flowing almost right to the step pyramid known as the Monument of the Ancients before dispersing.
entities.short_description: The Alaphaer Run was a fast-flowing, supernaturally cold river that found in the Moonsea North region of North Faerûn.

entities.name: Alarangh
entities.description:
Alarangh was a bandit keep, taken by the Zhentarim in .

Alarangh was south of the East Way and just east of the Thunder Gap.

As of , Alarangh was under Zhentarim control, per Fzoul Chembryl.

In , Fzoul Chembryl reported to Xarlraun, a beholder, that the bandit keeps of Alarangh and Tossril were now under Zhentarim control, and forces were dispatched from there to assist in the capture of Shandril Shessair. The force out of Alarangh was twenty men strong.
entities.short_description: Alarangh was a bandit keep, taken by the Zhentarim in .

entities.name: Alaron
entities.description:
Alaron, also known as Westshae was the most populous island in the Moonshae Isles.

The island was roughly divided in half by the Fairheight Mountains, which trapped rains and clouds on the northern side of the island as they blew in from the Trackless Sea, and shielded the southern side from the ocean harsh storms. The southern part of Alaron was further moderated by the currents of the Sea of Swords, and was a fertile land of grassy low hills and dales ideal for farming. The northern half was rocky and steep, save for some grassy hills in the central region, with its weather being mostly dictated by the stormy seas. The largest city on the island was Caer Callidyrr, located on the northern edge of Dernall Forest.

The southern half of the island traditionally comprised the Ffolk Kingdom of Callidyrr, ruled from the capital city of Caer Callidyrr. With the rise of High King Tristan Kendrick in the mid–14 century DR, Caer Callidyrr became the capital of all Ffolk realms in the Moonshaes, and with the rise of High Queen Alicia Kendrick, it became the capital of the United Moonshae Isles in the . Alaron was thus considered the most powerful island prior to the Spellplague. However, with the decline of the unified kingdom, the Kendricks came to be kings and queens of only Alaron as of the late 15 century DR. The High King at this time was Derid Kendrick. The castle from which the Kendrick family ruled, the Palace of the High King, was built by the very first High King of Moonshae, Cymrych Hugh.

The northern half of the island comprised the Northlander kingdom of Gnarhelm, traditionally ruled from the city of Gnarhelm. As of the late 15 century DR, even as their kin in Norland had declared independence from the High King, Gnarhelm remained under Kendrick rule, its culture having become a blend of Northlander and Ffolk and its inhabitants coming to see themselves as Moonshavians rather than as Northlanders. The combined might of Callidyrr and Gnarhelm made Alaron effectively the most powerful kingdom in the Moonshae Isles.
entities.short_description: Alaron, also known as Westshae was the most populous island in the Moonshae Isles.

entities.name: Alashan
entities.description:
Alashan was a city located in the kingdom of Khazari within the Hordelands.

This important city sat along the banks of the Kuruk Muren river where the Silk Road passed through the western border of the country. Alashan was nestled into a pass where the steep Katakoro Shan mountains broke.

Alashan's position along the Silk Road caused great wealth to flow through the city. Many merchants and craftsmen called this city home.

Alashan's location offered strong natural defenses. In addition to these, strong fortifications were built, sheltering the city within from raiding horse bandits. A large gate house was complimented by towers located at each corner of the city, and a fortified palace dominated the center.

The typical price for room and board was 1 gp per person per night. Guests could expect to be charged twice or thrice this much if they caused damage or got violent.

Alathil was located in northern Haluraa south of the looming Nathaghal Mountains. The town sat along the north bank of the High Aluar river near its midpoint.

entities.name: Alatorin
entities.description:
Alatorin was the ancient dwarven settlement formed when Taark Shanat's dwarves defeated the inhabitants of Rringlor Noroth in the Cloaker Wars, including four blue dragons slain by Taark himself. It was the first settlement established in Shanatar and contained Brightaxe Hall and the famous Wyrmskull Throne.

Alatorin was founded at the end of the Cloaker Wars when Taark Shanat's dwarves claimed the caverns for themselves. It was captured by the drow of Guallidurth during the First Spider War ( to ), at which time the eight kingdoms of Shanatar allied to reclaim it.

The Second Spider War in saw the dwarves reclaim Alatorin from the drow, but the drow attacked again in the Third Spider War around . This conflict lasted around thirty years, with the eventual victory of the drow. Alatorin was evacuated by the dwarves (who took the Wyrmskull Throne with them).

entities.name: Albarrana
entities.description:
Albarranas were the fortresses used by efreet for defensive purposes that were scattered across their vast empire.

Each efreet thurgur could have up to four albarranas within its borders.

These fortresses were composed of rock, brick, and a special concrete made from volcanic rock.

Between 1,000 and 5,000 efreet soldiers were garrisoned at each albarrana. They were commanded by a single noble efreeti. When in the field, these heavily armed units were usually accompanied by special guides and scouts called dalil.

entities.name: Albottle Ferry
entities.description:
Albottle Ferry was a busy ferry crossing for the River Ashaba in the village of Wright's Ferry in Featherdale.

A team of large draft horses moved the ferry by means of ropes suspended over a timber frame.

The price to use the ferry was 7 sp per person which included a single mount plus another 3 sp for every additional pack animal. A wagon could be transported for 2 gp. The ferry was run by Dregan and Flender Albottle. Should a customer become unruly about the fares the brothers would call on their cousin Auglaer who was a massive man who appeared to have ogre blood in his veins.

entities.description:
The Albrazi Canal was a prominent canal located in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire in 1367 DR.

The canal branched west from the Great Canal in the Pyraculum near the center of the city, turned southwest at the borders of the Rookery and Iskalat, and continued through Iskalat until it emptied into the north side of the harbor. It passed under the Street of the Craftsmen and Street of the Vine along the way.

As with all canals within the City of Brass, the Albrazi Canal was filled with lava from the Sea of Fire

entities.name: Alchemical Seminary
entities.description:
The Alchemical Seminary was a famous school of alchemy and transmutative magic in Eileanar, the enclave of Karsus.

The school was found on the outer southeast edge of Eileanar, near the Ancient Scrolls group.

The Seminary was the foremost institute in the fields of transformative magics and alchemical processes, being the finest in the enclave and all of Netheril. The master of the school was the venerable Quintus, while fiery transmutations were taught by Hakewill, watery subjects by Cujas, airy magics by Thibauneau, and earthy transformations by Fries. Delacroix was the master of potions, oils, and other liquid products, while Colombier was an expert in magical powders and dusts.

entities.name: Aldani Basin
entities.description:
The Aldani Basin was a huge, swampy drainage basin in the middle of the jungles of Chult.

This upland basin was surrounded on all sides by high plateaus and had multiple secluded lakes where its waters gathered. The central region of the basin was swampland, surrounded by thick foliage. The basin was large enough to be seen with the naked eye as a gap in the jungle canopy from 20 miles away if one stood atop the Firefinger, a 300-foot tall natural rock formation.

The Aldani Basin was a favored feeding ground for all kinds of dinosaurs and biting insects.

The basin received its name from the Aldani, "lobsterfolk", living there and in the two major rivers flowing from it. At one time, they lived in the rivers, but in later years, they had retreated back to the lakes.

Circa 1491 DR, the farm was owned and ran by Qelline Alderleaf. She was willing to let adventurers sleep in the farm's hayloft.

entities.name: Aldever's Street
entities.description:
Aldever's Street was a major road in Luskan's South Bank.

Aldever's Street began at the south wall of the city at Captains' Court, which sat on the north side of the road opposite the Hall of Warriors temple. It ran northwest to Captains' Close, where it intersected the Darkwalk. It then turned north between Captains' Close on the east side and the Ruins of Illusk on the west before ending at the city market. The road continued eastward as Setting Sun Street.

As of the mid-to-late 14 century DR, Aldever's Street was a notably safe road by Luskan's standards, owing to the Luskanite soldiers standing guard at Captains' Court and the Hall of Warriors. Whenever Luskan mustered for war, Aldever's Street was the site of soldiers marching in formation as they made their way to the temple for mandatory prayers to Tempus.

entities.name: Aldreth
entities.description:
Aldreth was the largest of the river ports along the coast of the Sword River in the Sword Lands, Laerakond, as of 1479 DR.

Aldreth was considered to be the most sophisticated of the Sword Lands towns, and the most snooty by envious people of other towns. The merchants of Aldreth fancied themselves as the true lords of the Sword Lands because their great wealth.

Aldreth was the most wealthy of the towns along the Sword River, with the best markets and a great variety of goods, travelers, and strange curios from afar.

The lord of the town was chosen by the wealthy Aldran merchants, who decided who would take that appointment through financial support and careful assassination.

entities.name: The Ale and Rabbit
entities.description:
The Ale and Rabbit was an inn and bathhouse in the halfling village of Shining Falls in the Delimbiyr Vale in the 14 century DR.

It was one of the biggest and tallest buildings in the small village.

The only inn in the last village up the Delimbiyr River, The Ale and Rabbit served the majority of inhabitants. It was also the last stop for the trappers and explorers that went north, and probably the first for those that returned.

Guests could stay the night in the large common room for 5 sp or in a pricey private room for 3 gp. The inn also provided several baths; these were free with an overnight stay or could be rented separately for 5 sp.

Ale Street was located in Zhentil Keep's Common Quarter in the eastern section of the city. The road connected Beholder Street with the Street of Sorrow. Black Street intersected Ale Street near its midpoint.

This kingdom occupied the eastern leg of the Alamber Sea, which made up a large portion of that sea,

The exact location of the kingdom was a mystery to the surface dwellers of the Old Empires, though they mistakenly believed it to lay somewhere north of the Ship of the Gods.

The kingdom of Aleaxtis was founded in the year , by the sahuagin T'Raam. His reign would go on for 297 years.

entities.name: Algid
entities.description:
Algid was a small town on the shore of Hidden Lake, as part of the Netherese Empire.

Algid was situated on the southern coast of the Hidden Lake, between the Southfill River and Tarn River.

Algid was built by thirty workers in , and grew very slowly until , when it reached a peak population of one thousand inhabitants, firmly remaining a sleepy fishing village. During the Age of Discovery, the talented arcanist, Lady Polaris, approached the townsfolk and offered them enclave status. However, the residents much preferred being part of Low Netheril, and thus refused the arcanist's offer.

During the Shadowed Age, the inhabitants began to increase their usage of magic. Some of the residents became very skilled in the Art, and even used spells such as Yturn's levitation and Tolodine's gust of wind in order to create magical airships to patrol Hidden Lake. In , Algid was destroyed by the phaerimm, leaving barely any alive. Those who did survive were offered residency in nearby settlements.

entities.name: Ali-bin-Jafar's Textiles
entities.description:
Ali-bin-Jafar's Textiles was a shop in the Central Trade Lanes of Skullport in the late 14 century DR.

Ali-bin-Jafar's Textiles was a two-story establishment of fair condition, marked at its entrance by a brightly patterned curtain.

The interior functioned as a warehouse for a wide variety of fabrics, threads, and rare carpets sourced from regions such as Kara-Tur, Calimshan, Zakhara, and the Hordelands.

Alongside regular trade in textiles, the shop also served as a conduit for contraband. Bolts of inexpensive cloth frequently concealed smuggled items moved in collaboration with the Xanathar's Thieves' Guild and Misker.

entities.name: Alimir Mountains
entities.description:
The Alimir Mountains served as the eastern border of Calimshan and were once the home of a great horde of beholders.

The Alimir Mountains composed the southern end of the Iltkazar Range, the same chain of mountains containing the Omlarandin Mountains, the Kuldin Peaks, the Snowflake Mountains, and the Giant's Run Mountains. The mountains ran down into the Lake of Steam in the east and extended into the Shining Sea in the south in what was known as the Alimir Peninsula. The waters around the Alimir contained pearl beds.

The Alimirs were not surrounded by gradual foothills as were the more northerly mountains in the Iltkazar Range; they exploded out of the ground with steep sides. After a few thousand feet in height, most of the trees gave way to exposed rock, and the steep slopes began to level off only after around 4,000 feet (1,200 meters) on average. The majority of the peaks had summits above 6,000 feet (1,800 meters) over sea level.

The two tallest peaks were Mount Kahdas (7,800 ft or 2377 m) and Mount Phevos (8,500 ft or 2591 m), which were located in the middle of the range. The sheer faces of these two peaks were known as the Eye Tyrant Cliffs, for here was the site of an epic battle between the humans of Calimshan and an army of beholders in the ancient past. The cliffs were carved with intricate artwork depicting the battle, which could be seen from a great distance away.

The school was located in Seventon, Netheril.

This academy taught mentalism, one of the Fields of Mythal. The owner and tutor was Alimon.

Enollar the arcanist enrolled at the institute in . He quickly became the top student, and left with a wealth of knowledge to travel around the rest of Netheril.

The All Faiths Altar was a shrine in the city of Loudwater in the Delimbiyr Vale in the mid-to-late 14 century DR. It was open to worshipers of all non-evil faiths (with Bane, Cyric, Malar, and such excluded).

Poor travelers sometimes slept in the shrine's forechancel, usually when the weather was bad. However, pilgrims and wandering priests were permitted to stay no more than a tenday.

All Faiths Hall was a place of worship in the city of Everlund.

All Faiths Hall was established for the worship of any of the good deities.

entities.description:
The Allascar was a great valley in Turmish in the Vilhon Reach.

Lying in the southwestern reaches of Turmish, the Allascar cut westward into the great Orsraun Mountains.

On a side-trail a little way beyond the lip of the Allascar, on the steep slope down to the great Faraway forest, stood the isolated inn of The Five Lions.

entities.description:
The Allegro River was a river in the High Ice region of Netheril.

Located in the frigid High Ice region, the Allegro River fed the Nyanza Lake to its north.

Schools of salmon were known to live in the river and thus the Allegro River became known as one of the best salmon fishing spots.

The cold river was not often visited by those of the Netherese Empire, as they couldn't stand the freezing temperatures. However, some fishermen specifically went to the Allegro River for its abundance of fish. Approximately half of the fishermen would never return, however, because of hypothermia and frostbite, as well as remorhaz and bear attacks.

The Alley of the Booksellers was a small but important street in Rog'osto in 1367 DR.

Many researchers and wizards frequented the Alley of the Booksellers, patronizing the many shops offering books and scrolls for sale. The selection of reading material available here was stocked with selections from all regions of Zakhara.

Several prominent sages lived on the street, selling books and offering their expertise in order to fund their own research.

entities.description:
The Allfaiths Shrine was a non-denominational, wayside shrine in the village of Red Larch.

The shrine was situated on the western side of the Long Road, south of the Swinging Sword Inn.

The shrine was constructed of stone and said to resemble a grand mansion. At its entrance were two wide wooden doors, each painted with the holy symbols of numerous gods.

The interior of the shrine was rather plain and had a simple stone altar. In the back of the shrine were two rooms for visiting priests to sleep in.

entities.name: Alliance of Seventon
entities.description:
The Alliance of Seventon was a confederation south of the Narrow Sea in north Faerûn in the 4 millennium before Dale Reckoning. It was a precursor to the nation of Netheril. Destroyed by orks in 3502 NY.

The First Age (0-325 NY): The citizens of seven fishing villages on the Narrow Sea—Fenwick, Gers, Gilan, Gustaf, Moran, Nauseef, and Janick—sought mutual protection and chose to unite, forming the Alliance of Seventon. To mark and celebrate this union, they created the Netheril Year calendar, with the year of founding being . They sought protection from orks, that where threatening their existence. An alliance with nearby living elves was formed. The elves taught them how to use rudimentary magic. The First Age ended with the beginning of the expansion of the union.

The shaman king Nether the Elder of Gers demanded ever greater tributes from the seven villages. In , the alliance expanded into an empire named Netheril, meaning "Nether's Land", now a kingdom under Nether's rule.

After the alliance expanded to become an empire, the name "Seventon" was from then on used as the location of the original group of villages.

entities.description:
Allis Lhyssich's Hand Crafted Weapons and Magical Weapons for Noble Causes was a specialist weapons store that also had standard gear for sale.

The shop was located close to the south gate of Neverwinter.

The master blacksmith, Allis Lhyssich, was one of the few smiths able to create magical weapons with meteorite ore. The crafting procedure took three days to make these highly enchanted meteorite weapons.

entities.name: Allyn's Anvil
entities.description:
Allyn's Anvil was an ancient stone circle situated high in the northern Alimir Mountains between Calimshan and the Lake of Steam. It lay east of St. Wityn's Hospice.

The site consisted of a semi-circle of stone boulders, all long-shattered as if by some titanic explosion, half-buried by grass and brambles. At the center was the Anvil itself: a pair of megaliths, one lying on top of the other, amidst patches of nettles. The upper stone was black and marbled all over with white stripes—this type of stone was unique, not found anywhere else in the Iltkazar Range.

Legend told that uncounted artifacts were forged upon the Anvil. It was considered to a sacred site by those churches who valued justice, in particular the church of Tyr.

Sometime in the 1st century DR, Tyr the Just God appeared at Allyn's Anvil and consecrated the Demonsbane shields.

entities.name: Almaes the Alchemist's shop
entities.description:
Almaes the Alchemist's Shop was the shop of the gnomish alchemist Almaestaddamir Auldcastle found in Ashabenford, Mistledale, in the late 1300s DR. Within his lab, he produced and sold a variety of alchemical reagents and completed mixtures. Among these were smokepowder, tanglefoot bags, sunrods, and various acids and anti-toxins.

On one occasion, Almaestaddamir made an offer to High Councilor Haresk Malorn to build a machine capable of flinging kegs of smokepowder at drow raiders in order to better defend the dale. The latter politely declined the proposal.

entities.name: Almorel
entities.description:
Almorel was a cosmopolitan yet primarily human trade city on the Golden Way.

Almorel was located on the southeastern shores of the Lake of Mists where the Golden Way ran alongside it. It was the last caravan stop before entering the Endless Waste.

Almorel was a sprawling town, buildings were almost all built out of wood and designed to be low and wide, with most households having attached stables and barns (so it wasn't necessary to go outside during the cold winters) as well as gardens and workshops. It was extremely rare for any building to have more than two stores. Wealthy families erected stockades around their properties.

The gold dwarves of Almorel lived in a series of tunnels beneath the city. Traditionally, humans were not allowed down in the tunnels but the dwarves had set up small guest houses to receive human visitors. The dwarves did not speak openly about their underground homes which elicited much rumormongering of the secrets the dwarves kept down there.
entities.short_description: Almorel was a cosmopolitan yet primarily human trade city on the Golden Way.

entities.name: Almraiven
entities.description:
Almraiven was one of the great cities of the nation of Calimshan. It was most notable for being the nation's first and premier center for magical studies, until the late 15 century DR, when the region's enslaved populace rose up and overthrew their tyrannical genie-kin rulers.

Almraiven was on the south-western shores of Calimshan, a port of the Shining Sea. It was close to the Spider Swamp and Alimir Mountains.

Almraiven was built using the "drudach system", This Calishite form of urban structuring, established all the way back to when the land was ruled by genies, consisted of an interlocking series of small brick-walled neighborhoods called drudachs. All drudachs were further grouped together into subdivisons known as sabbans, whose boundaries were similarly marked by low mud-brick walls. Each sabban worked as a self-sufficient town—it had its own water supplies, guards, markets, residences, and so on. The city had a total of 12 sabbans and 49 drudachs.

The largest of these sabbans was the Mage's Quarter. Located in the center of the city, it was comprised of seven drudachs.

entities.name: Almraiven Peninsula
entities.description:
The Almraiven Peninsula was a rocky peninsula in west Faerûn's Lands of Intrigue region, named after the mountain chain that was part of it - the Alimir Mountains.

This peninsula was within the borders of both eastern Calimshan and eastern Tethyr. It included the Qartan Hills and eastern expanse of the Darthiir Wood that stretched alongside it. It was framed by the Shining Sea to the south and the Lake of Steam to the north.

At the height of Shanatar's power in -8100 DR, the Underdark depths of the Almraiven Peninsula were within its borders.

entities.name: Alnether Street
entities.description:
Alnether Street was a road that was located in the city of Waterdeep.

Alnether Street was located in the northern section of Waterdeep's Castle Ward. The road orignated on Bazaar Street, branching south where it ran parallel to the Street of Silver to the west and Warrior's Way to the east. Alnether Street merged with the western end of Cymbril's Walk near the Street of Silver's intersection with Keltarn Street. The Prowl branched off the southeast end of Alnether Street.

entities.name: Alonmarch
entities.description:
Alonmarch was a county in Duchy Suretmarch in eastern Tethyr.

Alonmarch was located just where the lowlands and the highlands of Tethyr met.

In 1370 DR, Count Vartan Thrynnar ruled Alonmarch from his castle of Thynnar's Hold atop Komar's Hill.

Alonmarch was one of the few stable areas of the country during the unrest of the Tethyrian Interregnum, because Count Vartan Thrynnar went out of his way to protect his tenant peasants, permitting some of them to even take refuge in Thrynnar's Hold.
entities.short_description: Alonmarch was a county in Duchy Suretmarch in eastern Tethyr.

entities.name: Aloum Lyndren
entities.description:
Aloum Lyndren was a leaf farm owned by Tatha Beruel in west Faerûn circa the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR.

Tatha's farm was located a few miles west of Elturel on the northern side of Skuldask Road. The walls of the city could be made out in the distance from atop the hill closest to Elturel overlooking the ranch owned by Elmair Broruk. The property extended back from the road (northward) over another hill about two miles (a little over three kilometers) away and ended at the Gnaw Rocks, which marked the border of her land with the livestock farm that belonged to the Trindle family. To the west, over a third hill, was grazing land that belonged to the cattle breeder Ohlongh Vrurr. South across the road was more of Elmair Broruk's ranch.

A natural spring made this site ideal for habitation and Tatha's underground home was located a short way downhill from its stone-lined catch-basin. Her dwelling had a sod roof that was covered with an herb garden and her barn (also mostly underground with an herb garden on the roof) was in a similar small clearing connected by a short path through sparse trees. Runoff from the spring and waste water from her sink were piped to a small swampy area in the lowest corner of her property.

Thicker stands of trees covered most of the land, but three larger clearings scattered around the farmstead showed that the forest was being lightly harvested and new trees planted to replace them. Mostly oak trees formed the southern border along Skuldask Road and up the eastern hill known as Vixen Rise. To the west were predominantly maple trees climbing up the slope of Sundown Rise. Following one of the small trails northward, a visitor saw mostly blueleaf trees until the summit of Dark Rise. On the far side of that hill to the Gnaw Rocks were mainly hazel, ash, and hornbeam trees.

entities.name: Aloushe
entities.description:
Aloushe was a secretive and independent realm of dryads in the forests of Cormyr.

The realm lay somewhere not far east of Waymoot in the King's Forest.

At some point during his time as Royal Magician, Vangerdahast discovered the realm via his long-range scrying magic. He delivered a challenge to the inhabitants that was answered by Queen Radanathe, who asserted her realm's independence from Cormyr.

entities.name: Alphar
entities.description:
Alphar, also known as Alphar Port, was the largest settlement on Alphar Isle in the Pirate Isles on the Sea of Fallen Stars

Alphar was located on the western coast near the middle of the island.

It had the largest harbor on Alphar Isle, being able to hold 30 ships, and was a flourishing town almost 5,000 people circa 1359 DR.

Unlike the other settlements scattered though the Pirate Isles, Alphar had its own government separate from the influence of any pirate captains. This government was headed by Selshin Toshant in the 1350s DR. Although a retired pirate himself, he worked to "clean up" the harbor, tried to ban wanted pirates, and attempted to initiate legal trade with the northern nations of Sembia, Procampur, and Impiltur. However, they were not enamored of establishing such bonds with a port that had close ties to pirates and, at home, the folk of Alphar held tight to their pirate traditions and opposed Selshin's efforts. There was a risk that if he pushed too far, he would be removed from power before long.

entities.name: Alphar Isle
entities.description:
Alphar Isle was an island in the Pirate Isles in the Sea of Fallen Stars.

The island lay just east of the northeastern stretch of the Windrace, a strait known for its strong prevailing winds. It enabled speedy sailing from the Bowl in the heart of the Pirate Isles to Alphar Isle and beyond, but made the return journey quite difficult and time-consuming. Another strait, called the Spoon, ran from Alphar Isle's southern coast to Ilthan and back to the Bowl.

Alphar Isle was only slightly smaller than the Dragonisle and had a greater area of usable land, but was actually less attractive as a pirate port, owing to its less defensible and smaller harbors. Moreover, it was too close to Procampur and Tsurlagol in the Vast, allowing their ships to make patrols and raids with ease, and too far from the trade routes to Chessenta, Mulhorand, and Thay, unlike the Dragonisle.

There were several harbors on the island,

entities.name: Alpuk
entities.description:
Alpuk, also called the Central Basin, was the largest of the three regions of the Great Glacier and the home of the Iulutiun people.

The Great Glacier was naturally divided into three regions. The largest region was Alpuk, located in the southwest and bordered by the Uppuk River in the north, the Tuutsaas Chain in the west, the Lugsaas Chain in the south, and the Keryjek Ridge in the east. The region of Angalpuk was to the east, and Nakvaligach to the north.

Alpuk encompassed the two largest seas in the Great Glacier, the Nakalpgotak and the Lugalpgotak. The mysterious mountainous region known as Novularond, home of frost giants and arctic dwarves, was also within its borders.

Most of the land was at a low elevation, but the ground was rough and occasionally contained rolling hills.

entities.name: Alsapir's Rock
entities.description:
Alsapir's Rock was a tiny island in the Red Rocks in the Sea of Swords of the Sword Coast North. Notably, it was once the lair of the copper dragon Gaulauntyr, called Glorytongue.

Part of the Red Rocks archipelago, it lay just north of Waterdeep and so near the coast and Mount Sar that it was rarely marked on maps and sea charts.

On its western side was a many-branched sea cave carved out by the waves, with tidal waters flooding its entrance. Here was where Gaulauntyr had made her lair. Although she had moved away by 1372 DR, she left behind her food source—a captive deepspawn that produced boars, deer, rothé, and sundry other prey animals to satisfy her appetite. Unfortunately, while the deepspawn kept birthing them, there was no food for them and no way out of the caves, so they simply starved and died.

It acquired its name after a fisherman called Alsapir met his death here when a storm smashed his boat against the rock.

entities.description:
Altand was a village in the Misty Forest in the Western Heartlands in the late 15 century DR. The village existed on two levels, with a few structures built on the ground around an ancient monument to an elven ranger.

Residences and the village temple were built into the upper boughs of the forest. The elves strung rope bridges between these sites and constructed circular walkways around the trees.

entities.name: Altar of Scales
entities.description:
The Altar of Scales was a temple dedicated to Tiamat, the Dragon Queen within the Untheric pantheon.

The temple lay within the catacombs beneath the ruins of Unthalass in Unther.

The Altar of Scales survived the destruction of Unthalass when Tiamat and Gilgeam battled through the city, flourishing in the anarchy that ensured with the city's destruction. The leader of the temple at this time was High Priestess Shudu-Ab.

entities.name: Altar of Shields
entities.description:
The Altar of Shields was a shrine dedicated to Helm in the city of Tilverton in Cormyr in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

The Altar stood on a covered landing along the north-western Cormyr Stairs that connected the city's lower city and the Old Town.

entities.name: Altar of the Air
entities.description:
The Altar of the Air was a shrine to the goddess Akadi built over a crypt in the center of the ruins of the city of Dashadjen.

The mummified priestess of Akadi, El Sadhara, resided there.

Some unknown power protected the shrine from the destructive power of the sands of the Calim Desert, and the Altar and its tombs below were said to contain treasures and magic unimaginable.

The structure was built by lesser djinn during the time of Coramshan to honor the djinni Calim, and much of its elemental treasures awaited his supposed return.

entities.name: Altarea's Needles
entities.description:
Altarea's Needles was a seamstressing and waterproofing house in the Dock Ward of Waterdeep in the mid–14 century DR.

Tessaril Winter expected someone, almost certainly Harpers, to be operating there.

In the , Narm Tamaraith and Shandril Shessair were instructed by Tessaril Winter to ask for "the little lady that does the pearls" at the shop when they arrived in Waterdeep.

entities.name: Altumbel
entities.description:
Altumbel was a secluded nation of fishermen and merchant-pirates located on the peninsula that extended into the Sea of Fallen Stars. By choice, its people became isolationists and had little relations with nearby Aglarond or other neighboring countries.

The county neighbored Aglarond to the east and included the Thousand Swords among its territory.

Altumbel's harsh landscape was dotted with temperate, wind-swept valleys that were not suitable for farming. There were no forests in the region.

The coastline was shrouded in fog, obscuring a rocky descent into the sea. The cold waters were rich with sea life.

Alu was located on the coast of southwest Halruaa. The town lay along the shore of the western half of the Bay of Taertal on the Great Sea.

entities.name: Aluianti
entities.description:
Aluianti was a village of gold elves in Semberholme.

Aluianti was one of the smaller settlements within the region, typically housing no more than fifty residents at any given time. The village boasted an exclusive populace of gold elves, although it remained open and welcoming to all elves.

At the heart of Aluianti's cultural identity lied its artisans, whose creative endeavors garnered widespread admiration. The inhabitants of the village were primarily skilled artisans, channeling their expertise into crafting exquisite pottery, exceptional paintings, and masterful jewelry adorned with precious gems. Aluianti's artistic offerings have earned it a reputation for producing works of unparalleled beauty and craftsmanship.

Aluianti was established in The Year of Tomes, -54 DR. Seeking respite from the tumultuous political climate in Cormanthor and driven by concerns for the clan's prosperity, the influential heads of the Aluianti families made the pivotal decision to relocate to this idyllic locale.
entities.short_description: Aluianti was a village of gold elves in Semberholme.

entities.name: Aluwand
entities.description:
Aluwand () was the capital city of Selu'Maraar, a sea elf kingdom beneath the waves of the Dragon Reach.

In relation to the surface world, Aluwand was located roughly east of the Scar,

This city was the seat of power for the ruler of Selu'Maraar, who held the classical Faerûnian elf title of Coronal.

Aluwand was constructed around by refugees of Cormanthyr, who had transformed themselves into sea elves through use of the artifact known as the Sashelan Glass. It later became incorporated into Selu'Maraar, but would not become its capital until much later.
entities.short_description: Aluwand () was the capital city of Selu'Maraar, a sea elf kingdom beneath the waves of the Dragon Reach.

entities.name: Alyssim
entities.description:
Alyssim was a tiny elven village located about fifty miles to the east of Essemore on the banks of the Elvenflow.

The people of Alyssim frowned upon half-elves and punished any elves who procreated with other species. Females were looked down upon in Alyssim society. The villagers worshiped Rillifane Rallathil, and recognizing other deities was also frowned upon.

Alyssim's most notable former inhabitant was Lyra Sunrose, a half-elf who was shunned in the village and later became friends with Elminster.

As of 1367 DR, the village no longer existed and its former site was overrun with stinkweeds, although the exact date and cause of its demise were not known.
entities.short_description: Alyssim was a tiny elven village located about fifty miles to the east of Essemore on the banks of the Elvenflow.

entities.name: Ama Basin
entities.description:
The Ama Basin was the southern part of the land called the Northern Wastes in Kara-Tur. This land was called the Ama Basin in honor of the great river Ama that originated here and ended in the Celestial Sea. Also in these lands were the Koryaz Mountains, which were home to many tribes.

The Ama Basin was a large, mostly unexplored area consisting of woodlands and swamps, rich with game.

It was believed that the least explored part of the Ama Basin's great forests grew on the land that was the site of collapsed expansive mines used in the ancient times.

In the decades following the Spellplague, several powerful onis living in this basin enslaved hobgoblins from the nearby Land of the Snow Spirits, posing a constant threat to the human villages scattered around the region.

entities.name: Ama River
entities.description:
The Ama River was fed by all water draining from Ulhai Shan to the north and west, and the Chigiogi Mountains to the south. It flowed west to east, eventually draining into the Yellow Sea. The river flooded during spring to the point of being unrecognizable from the surrounding marshland. It froze solid during the winter months, creating a highway for the forest tribes.

Many spirit folk haunted the depths of the great river.

entities.name: Amah
entities.description:
Amah was a city-state of the Free Cities of the Vilhon Reach that maintained neutrality between Turmish and Chondath. Along with the cities of Nleeth, and Reth, they were sometimes referred to as the Southsands Games.

Amah was settled in , originally to be used as a neutral training center for mock-battles Turmish and Chondath. The cities of Nleeth and Reth, served the same function, one allied with Turmish, while the other with Chondath. Both were established the same year. After the mining town of Aelor exhausted its gold production, it lost its population to the neighboring city of Amah.

In 1358 DR, the Mayor of Amah at the time - Pachipol, participated in a meeting of leaders of both Chondath and Turmish to discuss the menace of the arcanaloth Yrkhetep.

As of 1370 DR, Amah and Nleeth were still used as training centers for outside armies, however bloodshed of the towns' past was abandoned. The visiting armies of Turmish and Chondath clashed in competitions of combat mettle and tactics.

entities.description:
Amalae's was a beauty shop in the Southern Ward of Waterdeep.

This building stood at the northwestern end of the culdesac The Boomgarden.

The proprietors of this shop offered baths, hair-washing, hair-stylings, "touches" (manicures and pedicures), and other cosmetic applications within separate rooms of the building.

Additionally, those who worked here would offer patrons a fee to share a bed with them for the night or to rent out their attic. Some wizards were known to rent out this attic so they could conduct private spell-study.

The River Amarast wound through the jungles of Tashalar on the Chultan Peninsula of southwest Faerûn.

Originating in the Delphin Mountains, the River Amarast flowed southeast for approximately before emptying into the Lapal Sea in the heart of the jungle. It was the largest river in the jungle feeding the Lapal Sea.

The Amaratha Stream was a flowing body of water found in the grassy steppes of the Ride.

The stream flowed south from the White Peaks and wound southwest for miles before ending at a point just east of the Rogan's Sprint trail.

Amarathas were a variety of light green jewels unique to Faerûn.

entities.name: Amarune
entities.description:
Amarune was a small island found directly off the east coast of the kingdom of Gnarhelm within the Moonshae Isles.

Amarune sat just off shore from the mainland of Alaron where the unnamed river of the Lisloch emptied into the Sea of Swords. Amarune was small, covering just . There were no settlements of note found on the island.

A natural harbor, sheltered by a narrow opening through the mountains, was found on the island's western coast. Much of the island's exterior was framed with an unnamed mountain range, while the interior was covered with meadows and forests.

entities.name: Amazandar
entities.description:
Amazandar, also known as the City of Gems was the capital of the Lost Kingdom of Anauria.

Amazandar was located west of the Desertsmouth Mountains, due west of the peak Rausrawna, known as Mount Shaddath to the Anaurian people, southwest of Anauril, the City of Swords.

The city lay above rich veins of gems that could be reached by numerous deep shafts and tunnels.

As the capital of Anauria, Amazandar dominated trade between Anauria, and the other survivor-states of ancient Netheril, Asram, and Hlondath.

entities.name: Amberforge
entities.description:
The Amberforge was a smithy in the Central Trade Lanes of Skullport in the late 14 century DR.

The Amberforge was a one-story building in fair condition.

The owner of the Amberforge, Amber Smithkin was known for her no-nonsense demeanor and an intolerance for disrespect, particularly in regard to her craft. Her reputation as a master of her trade, combined with her physically imposing presence, discouraged most from challenging her. However, customers who approached her with proper respect were rewarded with high-quality metal goods, including nails, horseshoes, pots, cauldrons, and various ironworking tools. The products she forged were durable and reliable, offered at average prices that reflect their solid workmanship.

entities.name: Amberside
entities.description:
Amberside was a large open market in Berdusk in the Western Heartlands in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

The market was located in the market quarter of Berdusk, just inside the city's northeast gate. The market was a maze of small tents and stalls of various colors, which were packed enough to be considered a good meeting spot for individuals who didn't want to be spotted by someone they knew.

Amberside was usually very busy, owing to the Berduskan traditions allowing its citizens to work quarter-shifts so that they could peruse the wares of the city's various shops.

The market stalls in Amberside mostly sold small, useful, and non-perishable wares, setting it apart from the more established businesses in the city that sold larger goods. Due to the heavy traffic from merchants and peddlers through Berdusk, Amberside's stalls and wares changed frequently, sometimes selling rare or exotic goods from other regions. There was also a fair amount of household ironmongery, as a result of the place being named for a blacksmith named Ilm Amberal at the market's edge.

entities.name: Ambletrees Arms
entities.description:
Ambletrees Arms was an inn of Athalantar in the 3 century DR.

Ambletrees Arms was on the northern side of the Delimbiyr River.

The kitchen had stairs up and a hearth. There was a cellar in the building, and a cesspit somewhere on the property.

There were drinkers, beds, and a kitchen; at least one traveler had her clothes cleaned and dried.
entities.short_description: Ambletrees Arms was an inn of Athalantar in the 3 century DR.

entities.name: Ambral Isle
entities.description:
Ambral Isle was an island in the Sea of Fallen Stars.

At some point before the founding of Waterdeep, Princess Elvandaruil's bracelet washed ashore after a flight spell failed on her.

Jokes at the expense of the intelligence of the inhabitants were common among the inhabitants of the Dragonmere, the Dales, and the Vast.

entities.name: Ambrara
entities.description:
Ambrara was the name of an inhabited settlement somewhere in Faerûn during the early-to-mid 8 century DR.

During the , the sage Beldrune told his fellow Tabarast that he had once been an actor in the original play version of The Stormy Knight, as the Second Undergardener, in Ambrara.

entities.name: Amcathra Villa
entities.description:
Amcathra Villa was the family estate of the Waterdhavian noble house Amcathra.

The villa was located in the central section of Waterdeep's North Ward in between the High Road and Ilzantil Street just north of Tarnath Street.

Amcathra Villa contained two buildings within the walled estate. The main building dwarfed the second building. They stood two and four stories tall.

entities.name: Amelior's workshop
entities.description:
This workshop was the residence of Amelior Amanitas when he lived in the village of Volkumburgh in 1358 DR.

This workshop was situated west of the village's inn, the Crimson Wyrm.

This workshop was a huge structure, towering over every other building in Volkumburgh. It had a heavy oakwood door, with an elegantly painted nameplate that read, "A. Amanitas — Alchemist." There was also a hidden door off to the side.

The frame of that main door was marked with many alchemical and magical symbols, as well as many copies of Amelior's personal sigil. Any attempts made to force the door open by physical or magical means would cause the perpetrator to be shrunken down to in height.

entities.name: Amern's Stables
entities.description:
Amern's Stables was a business for the care of horses in the city of Procampur in the Vast in the late 14 century DR. It was owned and run by Amern, a veteran trainer of horses.

entities.name: Amet'ned-thoth's Residence
entities.description:
Amet'ned-thoth's Residence was a private residence in the Lower Heart of Skullport in the late 14 century DR.

Amet'ned-thoth's Residence was a two-story building with a cellar maintained in fair condition.

The interior was decorated with carpets and tapestries in vivid, jewel-like colors intended to counterbalance the cavern's dim illumination. The entry hall and sitting room were furnished sparingly yet with refined taste.

Amet'ned-thoth was an avid collector of games of skill. His study featured a glass-fronted cabinet displaying finely crafted sets for chess, jackals and hounds, and table dice.

entities.name: Amkethran
entities.description:
Amkethran was a village embedded in an outcropping of rock in the Calim Desert in Calimshan in the 14 century DR.

Amkethran was partly built on several levels on a large rock. A large cave opening into the side of that rock was used as a cemetery, although when Gorion's Ward's party arrived it was magically sealed off as the lich Vongoethe had taken temporary residence in it.

The village in the Calim Desert was several hundred miles southwest of Saradush, with a direct path in between through the heart of the Forest of Mir and passing the Marching Mountains. A safer, but longer, route between Saradush and Amkethran by horse was four days west along the Ithal Road then a day south at Ithmong, reaching the edge of the Calim Desert in two days after passing the western tip of the Forest of Mir. On horse, Amkethran appeared by the early afternoon since entering the desert.

Although the village had a mayor, Omar Haraad, his position was mainly in name only, owing to the oppressive forces of the Bhaalspawn Balthazar. In 1368 DR, it was under the unofficial leadership of Balthazar, the leader of the local monastery. The village was in very bad shape, as its inhabitants lived in poverty and had to contend with Balthazar's mercenaries, who also lived there and did basically whatever they liked.

entities.description:
Ammakyl Flowers and Foods was a shop in the village of Amphail, selling fruits, vegetables, and trail baskets. It was run by the Ammakyl family of Waterdeep.

During the summer and autumn months, an awning was erected outside the shop to provide extra space for the wares. It sold skewered vegetables that had been dipped in gravy, and during the winter it imported fruit and vegetables from the Shining South, selling them at high prices, especially out of season.

Ammakyl Villa was the family estate of the Waterdhavian noble house Ammakyl.

The villa was located in the eastern section of Waterdeep's Sea Ward on Vondil Street with the west side of the villa touching Shield Street and the east side touching Copper Street.

There were four buildings within the walled estate with gardens in between. Two of the buildings were much larger than the others. Each building was one or two stories tall.

entities.description:
Ammarindar was a ruined city in the Northdark, inhabited by tanarukks in the late 15 century DR.

The city of Ammarindar was located primarily in the Northdark between the drow cities of Menzoberranzan and Ched Nasad. It was located in the region of the ancient dwarven kingdom of the same name that also included territory covering the upper Delimbiyr Vale, between the High Forest and the Fallen Lands.

Ammarindar was located some 250 miles southeast of Menzoberranzan and was linked to the city by dwarven tunnels carved over the Darklake.

The path through Ammarindar was considered the quickest journey between Menzoberranzan and Ched Nasad, but around the year 1372 DR, was less traveled because of the danger that lurked there.

The River Ammath flowed along the eastern edge of the Gnollwatch Mountains and north across the Hills of the Dead Kings before emptying into Melanith Bay near Hazuth, making it the largest river within the kingdom of Dambrath.

Ammathair Hawkfeather's residence was located in the west section of Waterdeep's Castle Ward on the western side of Swords Street just south of Keltarn Street.

entities.name: Ammathluir
entities.description:
Ammathluir was situated south of the Long Forest in western Luiren.

Though it boasted a population of 10,000 halflings, only a small fraction of the buildings of Ammathluir were found above ground, leading travelers to believe the city was just a simple village. Most of the population resided within halfoles underground.

A temple to Yondalla was built into the side of a hill in Ammathluir.

Many skilled woodcarvers and tradesmen lived in Ammathluir, drawing caravans from the nearby Great Trade Way.

entities.description:
Ammathtar was a city located in northeastern Dambrath,

Ammathtar was located between the Granuin forest on the east and the Trader's Way on the west.

Foreign travelers entering Ammathtar, including all adventurers, had to bribe an official with 100 gp each in order to enter the city. Prices for goods was discounted for crinti but inflated for every other race. A small percentage of all business transactions when to the city coffers, helping to fund a strong army.

The largest horse pens in all of Dambrath were found in Ammathtar, holding upward of 5,000 prized steeds.

The Ammathvale was a small open valley separating the Lluirwood in the north from the Southern Lluirwood in Luiren.

This region stretched west to east between the Trader's Way and the city of Ammathluir spanning roughly . An unnamed road branched off from the Trader's Way to pass through the Ammathvale, connecting the rest of the cities of Luiren.

entities.name: Amn
entities.description:
Amn (}}), also known as the Merchant's Domain, was a tremendously wealthy nation in West Faerûn. Prior to the Spellplague and the continent's disappearance, Amn held colonies far away in Maztica. Post-Spellplague it still controlled important trade routes to Calimshan and Baldur's Gate as well as colonial ports in the Moonshaes and Chult. Its population, mostly human with a large minority population of halflings, was historically in the range of 3 million. The country's natural resources and wealth, combined with its mercantile nature led Amn to become one of the most important and influential trading centers throughout Faerûn. The crowning jewel of this powerful state was the capital city of Athkatla, founded in 100 DR (0 in the rarely-used Amnian calendar) and often known as the "City of Coin."

Geographically, Amn was a fairly small state, though its size was impressive compared with its neighbor and frequent rival, Baldur's Gate. Historically, Amn held several colonies in Maztica but during the Spellplague these disappeared from Toril along with the rest of the continent. However, Amn remained a colonial power through the 15th century DR, primarily through its fortified ports in both Chult and the Moonshae Isles, as well as the Mhair Archipelago.

The weather was pleasant almost all the year round in Amn. At Lake Esmel, the temperature was warmer due to the hot springs. A diverse selection of crops grew very well in Amn, making for a surplus which was traded with other nations. Amn's rainy season was from Uktar to early Tarsakh. The winters were mild with minor freezes and a little snow all across the nation with the exception of Esmeltaran on Lake Esmel. Although the rivers froze over during Hammer, they did not harden enough to make crossing the ice safe. Due to blizzards in the Cloud Peaks over the winter, Nashkel could often become isolated from Athkatla.

Since its unification under Thayze Selemchant Amn was ruled by the Council of Six, who resided in Athkatla. Their main duties were to maintain trade within and outside of Amn, controlling nearly every aspect regarding the economy of the nation. Separate from their economic concerns, the council also coordinated the militaristic defense of the nation, a task in which each individual member had a particular role. These positions were anonymously held.

entities.name: Amnurflow
entities.description:
The Amnurflow was a river in Amn that flowed into Lake Weng.

The river was the northernmost of the tributaries of Lake Weng. It began in the Cloud Peaks west of Citadel Amnur. Midway to Lake Weng, it was joined by the Rashturiver from the east. Comassur Creek merged with the Amnurflow five miles northeast of the lake.

This river was named after General Amnur, a legendary military man who was the younger brother of the second king of Amn.

entities.name: Amnwater
entities.description:
Amnwater was a large town in Amn that acted as a vital caravan stop on the long trade route that ran between the east and west of the country.

The town sat at the meeting of the Lake Way, South Fork, Esmel Road, and Eshpurta Road, making it one of the most important crossroads in Amn.

The Wengwater flowed north of the city from the Cloud Peaks to Lake Weng. It flooded severely every spring, leaving a wide expanse of ponds that slowly evaporated over summer.

Amnwater was officially ruled by the High Wheel, who was responsible for overseeing the militia, defenses, and general infrastructure and welfare of the town. By the 14 century DR, the city was effectively owned and run by the Yhliivast, Wheelarit, and Ironseth families, who collectively dominated the businesses tied to the caravan trade.

entities.description:
Amphail was a village on the Long Road between Waterdeep and Red Larch.

It had a population of 600, supporting 250 more in outlying farms. The population was mostly humans, but there were a few half-elves, dwarves, halflings, and other races.

Amphail was named after one of Waterdeep's early warlords, Amphail the Just, who had estates here.

The village was three days' ride north of Waterdeep.

entities.name: Amphitheater
entities.description:
The Amphitheater in Oryndoll was located in the nexus tunnels, which connected five separate Ring Caverns. This was the largest gladiatorial arena in the city, and had several features in it that other arenas in the hive normally did not possess. The main use of the Amphitheater was in an event called a dominance tournament, which was a popular sport in the city.

Mind flayers that pitted their thralls against each another in a dominance tournament would stand on opposing twin platforms and entertained an audience of up to one thousand illithids at once. The arena also had crystals spread throughout the stands that were psionically attuned. These crystals enabled the audience to passively feel the sensations of the thralls as they were channeled through the illithid competitors during combat.

entities.name: Amphitheater of the First Thunder
entities.description:
The Amphitheater of the First Thunder was a temple and combat arena dedicated to Hoar, the Doombringer.

The temple was located in the capital city of Mourktar in Threskel.

The Amphitheater was a large open arena. The section of the compound that served as the temple was located underground.

Gladitorial matches occurred within the Amphitheater between the accused and accusers. These contests were used instead of a traditional court system as a form of justice. Hoar was believed to intervene in each match to ensure fitting justice was always served.
entities.short_description: The Amphitheater of the First Thunder was a temple and combat arena dedicated to Hoar, the Doombringer.

entities.name: Ample Chalice
entities.description:
The Ample Chalice was a rowdy tavern found in the fabled city of Myth Drannor.

It was located at the intersection of Moonshadows Street and Scatterhorn Street, in the Sheshyrinnam district of the city.

The Ample Chalice was one of the favorite haunts of the Akh'Velahr.

The boisterous Arnarra Gildenguard won ownership of the tavern in a game of chance. It quickly garnered a lot of business, becoming the tavern of choice for Ilphas Miritar, son of the city's Lord-Speaker.
entities.short_description: The Ample Chalice was a rowdy tavern found in the fabled city of Myth Drannor.

entities.name: Amra
entities.description:
Amra was an ancient human kingdom of Laerakond.

According to old legends, one of the kings that ruled Amra centuries before the Spellplague was a dragonheir. This king made Gauwervyndhal promise that she or any other dragon would never attack the Sword Lands.

Amra fell when the king was assassinated and the lords fought one another for the throne. Amra's castles and keeps were destroyed during the war.

Even after Amra fell, no dragon attacked the Sword Lands ever since.
entities.short_description: Amra was an ancient human kingdom of Laerakond.

entities.name: Amrani's Laundry
entities.description:
Amrani's Laundry was a business located in Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Amrani's Laundry was located in the central section of Waterdeep's Southern Ward within the Adventurers' Quarter. The front of the building lay along the west side of Slop Street, while the rear of the building faced Kolat Towers on Weeping Maiden's Run.

The business was owned by Amrani in the .

entities.name: Amruthar
entities.description:
Amruthar, also known as Burning Amruthar, was an independent city of east Faerûn that was located on the Eastern Way within the Thayan tharch of Lapendrar in the 14 century DR. It stood in defiance of High Regent Szass Tam, having previously been a puppet-state of the magocracy for centuries.

During the 10 century, the city of Amruthar was ruled by the powerful Mulhorandi satrap named Sekhotet. When the Red Wizards fought for their independence from Mulhorand in 922 DR, Sekhotet joined their rebellion on the condition he could rule his city by his own will. The Council of Zulkirs honored his wishes to the letter.

The city of Amruthar was devastated by the Spellplague of 1385 DR. The earthquakes that shook Thay split the land beneath the city, forming deep chasms that filled with rivers of lava.

The city lay about a tenday from the Yuirwood. The drow city of Brundag was roughly in the corresponding Underdark location.

entities.name: Amry
entities.description:
Amry was a coastal settlement found along the eastern stretch of the Dragon Coast, in the greater Eastern Heartlands of central Faerûn. It was located just north of the Gulthmere Forest, some ways west of Telpir.

The settlement of Amry was governed by a local council.

Along with the nearby settlement of Telpir, Amry enjoyed a good trading relationship with the Fellowship of the Purple Staff.

As of the , Amry was regularly imperiled by the bands of pirates that operated in the Sea of Fallen Stars.
entities.short_description: Amry was a coastal settlement found along the eastern stretch of the Dragon Coast, in the greater Eastern Heartlands of central Faerûn. It was located just north of the Gulthmere Forest, some ways west of Telpir.

entities.name: Amstel River
entities.description:
The Amstel River was a major river of eastern Amn that fed Lake Esmel.

This river served as a major route for barges from villages south of Eshpurta to Lake Esmel. The banks near the lake were made of the bright red clay of the region, and many villages profited from sales of pottery.

The bulk of the rivers waters came from the Khalleshyr and the River Valashar.

The river began 40 miles east of Trollford, where the River Valashar was joined by the Khalleshyr. After Trollford, it fused with the River Rimril, soon after the Rimril was itself joined by Trifin Creek at Eshpurta.

entities.name: Forest of Amtar
entities.description:
The Forest of Amtar (known as the Forest of Amlar to some Dambraii) was a large forest in south Faerûn.

During the Era of Upheaval, the Forest of Amtar was about 400 miles (650 kilometers) long and roughly 150 miles (240 kilometers) at its widest point. After the Spellplague, the Underchasm swallowed a portion of the forest and surrounded it on the west, north, and northeast sides. The Gnollwatch Mountains formed the forest's southern border. The River Ammath had its headwaters in Amtar and flowed eastward out of the forest. The River Dambron also began deep in the forest and flowed out southwest and around the Gnollwatch Mountains.

The Amtar Forest formed the northern border of the nation of Dambrath covering nearly half of its land area.

Before the Spellplague, the Landrise cut into the northeastern part of the forest, but the cliffs ended before reaching the other side. The eastern part of the forest hid many stone ruins of past cities, built by human-sized inhabitants as well as giant-sized, that made for break-neck drops and break-ankle ditches covered by profuse undergrowth.

entities.name: Anabravvur's
entities.description:
Anabravvur's was the best and most luxurious shipwright workshop in the Sea of Fallen Stars, based in Selgaunt of Sembia in 1490s DR.

By the late 15 century DR, Anabravvur's shipbuilders were run by Alpharra Anabravvur, the third generation of her family to helm the business. Alpharra's ships were huge and luxurious, elegantly designed out of superb materials. Anabravvur's received a lot of business but could afford to spend time on building, unaffected financially by the loss of one or more clients.

entities.name: Anadia
entities.description:
Anadia was the first planet from the Sun in Realmspace.

Due to its proximity to the Sun, most of Anadia's surface was too hot and dry to support humanoid life. The equatorial regions, which spanned 70% of the total surface area of the planet, were wastelands marked by enormous canyons which were inhabited mainly by umber hulks and other bestial life forms unique to the planet.

The north and south polar regions, however, supported a warm and humid climate that was favorable for humanoid life. These regions, where the halfling populations of the planet dwelt, were marked by rolling verdant hills that grew richer and denser in vegetation the closer one moved toward the poles. The central polar regions were also more mountainous, with the highest mountains being even snow-capped, from which sprung rivers that flowed toward the pastoral outer polar fields into lakes and freshwater seas. These seas in the north, named Footpond, Crystalsea, Bluewater, Frogspit, Squarelake, and Fingerwater, and 3 unnamed seas in the south never went too far out of these regions, evaporating quickly before reaching the torrid tropical zones.

There were two unique species of plants on Anadia: the poisonous powderpuff, which could be used to produce smokepowder; and the edible but not very nutritious crispyleaf, which could be employed as a gastric painkiller.

entities.name: Anai River
entities.description:
The Anai River was a river in the Plain of Horses region of northwestern Kara-Tur. It was the longest river in the region.

With headwaters in the Chigiogi Mountains and Chigidi Mountains, the Anai River meandered southward through the northern Chigidi Mountains. Next, it turned west and flowed through the northern taiga, where it divided into many branches and lakes that watered the woodlands and farms there. The two largest were Lake Gusang in the east and Lake Yetuq in the west, near the Torgny Branch.

Back in the mountains, however, another branch of the Anai flowed northward, entered the Ama Basin, and was one of the many tributaries of the great Ama River.

While the Anai River was easily navigable by boats in the warm season, it froze over in winter. This forced the use of carriages and sleighs pulled by horses along the ice itself, in order to transport goods and people.

entities.name: Anan
entities.description:
Anan was a village located in Miyama Province in Kozakura.

Anan was the ruins of a former village. The soldiers of the shugo-daimyo were responsible for its complete destruction, burning it to the ground. Prior to this event, Anan was a small, peaceful farming village.

The catalyst for this devastation was an incident in involving the son of a local farmer. In a shocking turn of events, he committed a grave act by striking down and killing the jito of the shoen. Following this act, he sought refuge in his parents' home. This decision was considered a severe transgression, particularly for a dutiful son. Compounding the situation, his parents, in a misguided act of protection, offered him shelter. This series of events ultimately led to the village's downfall, marking a tragic chapter in its history.

When the officials of the shugo-daimyo arrived at the village, the farmer's parents falsely claimed ignorance of their son's whereabouts, a sentiment echoed by the rest of the village. However, upon searching the village, the authorities found the criminal.
entities.short_description: Anan was a village located in Miyama Province in Kozakura.

entities.name: Anaster's Leatherworks
entities.description:
Anaster's Leatherworks was a leathergoods business in the city of Ordulin in the 14 century DR.

Anaster's sold a variety of different goods made of leather, including leather balls that came in , , and sizes.

Sometime in the mid–14 century DR, having took notice that Anaster's leather balls were more durable than any others made in Faerûn at the time, Aurora struck up an exclusive licensing deal with Anaster's to have her catalogue be the only business that could export their balls beyond the borders of Sembia.

entities.name: Anastur's Abrasives
entities.description:
Anastur's Abrasives was a prospecting and polish-making business in Llorkh in the 15 century DR.

Baelen Anastur sent out human and gnome prospectors across the Delimbiyr Vale to find particular minerals such as manganese and iron oxides, mixed with secret blends of oils to make fine abrasive polishes. It was linked by merchants' map to Samril's Fine Blades in Secomber, who used their polishes for finishing the raw blades of Arthane Furnace products such as longswords.

entities.name: Anathar's Dell
entities.description:
Anathar's Dell was an inn located in southern Daggerdale.

The establishment was nestled between Serpentsbridge to the north and the Spiderhaunt Woods to the south.

The Dell was settled by the dwarven Clan Brightblade, two old human families—Blacklock and Talop—and two half-elven families—Snowgold and Winterwood.

In spite of its size and relative exposure, Anathar's Dell was surprisingly well defended. Firstly, the farm family's borders were protected by ten or more trained hunting cats, which were fiercely loyal and attacked any non-humans or demihumans that got too close. Thanks to the dwarves, the farm folk were outfitted with arms and armor (ranging from chain mail up to plate mail) and could all be equipped rather quickly. In addition, the Dell had a few "secret defenses", among which included a potent sleep gas that was developed by the dwarves. The townsfolk become immune to its effects over many years of exposure resulting in a combination that often surprised many bands that thought the Dell easy prey.
entities.short_description: Anathar's Dell was an inn located in southern Daggerdale.

entities.name: Anauria
entities.description:
Anauria was one of a small number of enclaves that survived the fall of ancient Netheril. It grew into a great kingdom and the wealthiest of the Netherese survivor states before eventually being swallowed up by the growing Anauroch desert.

Anauria was one of Netheril's famed flying cities. It was famous for the craftsmanship of its swords and for its magic, and after the fall of Netheril, it became the richest of the three surviving states, collectively known as the Lost Kingdoms.

The cities of Anauria were located in the area of north Faerûn that was later known as the Sword, the southern region of the great Anauroch desert. Using landmarks from the Era of Upheaval, Anauria stretched from the Serpent Hills to the west, as far east as the Desertsmouth Mountains,

While Anauria was a human-ruled kingdom, its greatest ruler was King Thausimbel "The Wise" a great man of elven blood who ruled for over three and a half centuries.

entities.name: Anauril
entities.description:
Anauril, also known as the City of Swords was the one of the cities of ancient Anauria.

The city was located northeast of Amazandar the capital of Anauria, just due west of the Twisted Tower of Ashaba.

Anauril was famous for the great quality steels swords crafted by the finest smiths in all the lands north of the Moonsea. They were often granted enchantments by the mages of House Nyntynel and House Olyrnn.

The city was founded some time after Netheril's fall in , as the enclave of Anauria grew into a grand kingdom.
entities.short_description: Anauril, also known as the City of Swords was the one of the cities of ancient Anauria.

entities.name: Anauroch
entities.description:
Anauroch ( }} }}), also known as the Great Sand Sea or the Great Desert, was a desert in north Faerûn. The Anauroch formed due to phaerimm magic in the former region of Netheril, which was significantly different than the desert after. The name "Anauroch" once referred only to High Ice glacial region in the north, before it was applied to the whole desert.

Anauroch was bordered on the west by the Silver Marches, the Savage Frontier, and Evereska; on the south by Cormyr and south-east by the Dalelands; and on the east by the Moonsea and the Ride.

All of Anauroch was a desert and suffered harsh winters, but the regions of the desert had distinct climates. During the height of Shadovar rule, around , the temperatures were moderated and it rained in the region, Anauroch was commonly divided into three general regions: the northern High Ice, the middle Plain of Standing Stones, and the Sword in the south.

The High Ice was a frozen land of rocks and glacier. The Frozen Sea was often considered part of the High Ice, but its landscape was a maze of frozen sand dunes that melted during summer in the southern regions

entities.name: Anaxadren
entities.description:
Anaxadren was one of the Six Holy Cities of the ixitxachitl nation in the Sea of Fallen Stars known as the Xedran Reefs.

Like all of the 'chitl cities, Orilidren consisted of a huge warren of tunnels and subcaverns. This included a central entrance to the surface, with passages riddled in traps, and large cavern beneath that site with a great temple to Ilxendren around which the rest of the city grew outward from.

There stood an outbuilding near the temple for the Devitan's personal slaves, at least four caverns on the outskirts of the city in which other slaves were kept, two military garrisons, and at least four public shrines on the city outskirts that were dedicated to Ilxendren.

Anaxadren was located in the western reaches of the Xedran Reefs, standing to the east of the Haunted Plains and the ixitxachitl village of Ilsaadya.
entities.short_description: Anaxadren was one of the Six Holy Cities of the ixitxachitl nation in the Sea of Fallen Stars known as the Xedran Reefs.

entities.name: Ancestral mound
entities.description:
An ancestral mound, or ancestor mound, was a holy place of utmost important to the tribal peoples of Faerûn.

Every Uthgardt tribe had an associated mound, which was fixed at a specific location. Here, they believed their founders of tribe were buried, and worshiped totems, particularly during Runemeet. An altar mound, carved into the shape of a tribe's totem beast, was placed in the centre of an ancestral mound.

Multiple tribes could share their ancestral mound, such as the Black Lion tribe and Red Tiger tribe, whose ancestral mound was Beorunna's Well. Other known mounds were: Raven Rock, the Great Worm Cavern, Flint Rock, Morgur's Mound, Stone Stand, Shining White and the Grandfather Tree.

Most family groups, or clans of a specific tribe, would live only a few weeks trek from their ancestral mound.
entities.short_description: An ancestral mound, or ancestor mound, was a holy place of utmost important to the tribal peoples of Faerûn.

entities.name: Anchor Street
entities.description:
Anchor Street was a long thoroughfare in the Low City of Bral.

Anchor Street began at one of the ends of Dock Street and eventually ended upon Grand Street, along one of Low City's boundary points with Middle City, across from the Great Market. Along the way it was intersected by the ends of several streets. Eel Street, Hull Street, Sailmaker Street, Shipwright Street, and both ends of Round Street.

Along the span of buildings between Round Street's two ends, Anchor Street ran along the barrio known as Dracon-town. Additionally, two unnamed pathways descended from it, down to the Shipyards of the Rock.

entities.name: The Anchorage
entities.description:
The Anchorage was a cozy inn of well repute in Harrowdale.

The Anchorage was located near the center of town at the intersection of Melurk Street and Moonside Lane.

Each of the rooms of the Anchorage was practically sound proof thanks to thick stone walls and tapestries. Every room featured its own fire grate and enough furnishing to make a guest feel right at home.

Rooms at the Anchorage cost 14 sp per night per head, but that price included meals and stabling of a single beast. Any drink other than milk or mintwater cost extra, as did storing a wagon or stabling extra beasts.

entities.description:
Anchoret's Alley was a small side alley that was located in the city of Waterdeep.

Anchoret's Alley was located in the central section of Waterdeep's Southern Ward. It originated on the Forcebar where it branched south through a small neighborhood, eventually ending on Anchoret's Court just north of the Specterwalk.

entities.description:
Anchoret's Court was a small courtyard that was located in the city of Waterdeep.

Anchoret's Courty was located in the central section of Waterdeep's Southern Ward. It sat at the southern end of Anchoret's Alley just north of the Specterwalk.

A public well sat in the center of the courtyard.

The home of Kapplian Mulmastyr stood on the eastern side of Anchoret's Court near Caravan Street.

entities.name: Anchoril
entities.description:
Anchoril was a town on the island of Suj, located on its eastern shores, washed with the waters of the Trackless Sea. The closest major settlement to Anchoril was Sujjar, west of Anchoril, built on the Suj-lan bay.

Anchoril was connected to the Lantanna Embassy in Waterdeep via a keyed portal called The Welcome Gates. This two-way portal led to the Visitors' Vale just outside of Anchoril. The portal was protected by the key-word "Enjoy" and by Lantanna guards who deterred undesirables via dreaded bureaucracy.

entities.name: Anchorome
entities.description:
Anchorome (}}) was a continent on Toril. Sometimes referred to as the Anchorome Archipelago, it was a poorly known region composed of vast fertile lands and several islands. It constituted the northern portion of the large landmass in the planet's western hemisphere.

Anchorome was a vast land with numerous islands. It was located along the northwestern shore of the Trackless Sea, west of Evermeet and north of Maztica.

Northern Anchorome was described as an icy region.

Reports existed that northern Anchorome had been originally inhabited by aearee.

entities.name: The Ancient Scrolls
entities.description:
The Ancient Scrolls was a business that provided historical lore services in Eileanar, the famed enclave of Karsus.

The Scrolls were in the outer southwestern part of the city, very close to the Alchemical Seminary.

The five sages within the Scrolls had unique skills and areas of interest, and as a whole they specialized in the history of Netheril back to its First Age, as well as the recorded non-human societies that had existed during that time.

entities.name: Andamaar's Street
entities.description:
Andamaar's Street was a lesser avenue, paved in corduroy-logs,

Andamaar's Street marked the southern border of North Ward and the northern border of Trades Ward. It traveled from northwest to southeast, extending off of Zendulth Street and terminating at the High Road.

On the Trades Ward side, Andamaar's Street was met from the south by Lamp Street and Theln Lane, On the North Ward side of the street, Andamaar's acted as the western terminus of Undal's Lane.

When Waterdeep's walls expanded in 1101 DR to accommodate more settlers, the new perimeter approximated what would come to be the overall shape of Andamaar's Street.

entities.name: Andar's manor
entities.description:
Andar's manor was the residence of Andar in the village of Glen in Mistledale during the 14 century DR.

The manor lay a couple miles southwest of Glen, on a small hill; it was surrounded by an apple orchard.

The fieldstone house had several outbuildings.

It had a fireplace. Before it was raided, the house contained furniture.
