entities.name: Andlath
entities.description:
Andlath was a lost human kingdom that stood in the Shining Plains of the Vilhon Reach a thousand years before the 14 century DR.

Andlath's legacy was the Tethir Road, built between the (the year KingKing Dalagar "Longwalker" took the throne) and the . The road stretched from Athkatla in Amn to Ormath in the Shining Plains. Dalagar "Longwalker" attempted to unite South Faerûn through trade and expand Andlath's borders and influence. The tumultuous decade of building the road was filled with wars and strife caused by the project and attacks from elves and dwarves.

In the , Andlath lost control over its centaur slave population. Hearts of angry centaurs shattered the kingdom into a collection of scattered outposts and embattled besieged lands. King Dalagar personally helmed over forty battles in the course of a single year as the construction of the Tethir Road continued.

It was believed that Emperor Shoon IV of Calimshan was instrumental in the creation of the Tethir Road through magical means or political pressure.

entities.description:
Andora was a village of Auril-worshiping rangers and druids. It was protected by a magical gate.

entities.name: Andover Heights
entities.description:
Andover Heights was a small mountain range located on the island of Snowdown within the Moonshae Isles.

The mountain range stretched for roughly , running north to south along Snowdown's western coast with the Straight of Alaron. An unnamed forest and several lakes, including the Harloch, Mal Feargal, and Mal Sul, were found along the base of the eastern slopes. The inhabitants of the island also constructed several mines within Andover Heights.

entities.name: Anechu
entities.description:
Anechu was a village in the Ausa Province of T'u Lung. According to Tan Hikao Nong, it was a prosperous village whose inhabitants enjoyed a high quality of life unusual within T'u Lung, and it was for that reason that he considered it one of his favorite places.

It was situated along the northern bank of the upper Akensai River, where said river converged with an unnamed tributary. It was connected by road to the city of Chempka upstream and by trail to the villages of Honan and Chin as well as the city of Keeling.

As of , Anechu was led by Ho Kui Dung, a principled and trustworthy man who was a member of the same Ho clan that ruled over Ausa Province as a whole.

The Hearth Warmth, an inn which Tan Hikao Nong considered to serve the finest food within T'u Lung, was situated within Anechu.

entities.name: Al-Anf
entities.description:
Al-Anf, also called The Nose, was a small easterly island found in the Genie's Turban archipelago in the Corsair Domains of northwest Zakhara around 1367 DR.

Al-Anf and Al-Oyun were collectively referred to as the "Beauty Marks" by local corsairs. Ever distrustful of strangers, the corsairs would use the term as a form of password to test outsiders.

The island was the farthest southeast point of the Genie's Turban. It was a small forested island measuring roughly in diameter.

entities.name: Anga Vled
entities.description:
Anga Vled was a village of gnomes in the Fields of the Dead of the Western Heartlands, circa the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR.

This farming community was located on the north bank of the River Chionthar, west of Elturel. It took about a day to reach the village on horseback from Elturel.

Anga Vled was among the gnome settlements linked through the magical transportation network known as the Trail of Mists.

Anga Vled was on a caravan route and traded mainly in food. Produce from this village included asparagus, carrots, marrows, parsnips, and radishes. They also made a bread with spiced vegetables, and a very strong parsnip wine. Around 1370 DR, there were two gnomes skilled at training, shoeing, and healing horses. Occasionally, they had horses to trade or sell, typically when a merchant or traveler had to move on, leaving behind a sick or injured mount in their care. There was also a wheelwright, by name and by trade.

entities.name: Angalpuk
entities.description:
Angalpuk, also called the "Eastern Basin", was one of the three regions of the Great Glacier.

Angalpuk was located in the eastern Great Glacier. It was a very flat land with a scattering of mountains and forests.

Angalpuk had more vegetation than any other part of the Great Glacier, with small forests of birch, evergreens and willow. The trees rarely grew as tall as their southern cousins, usually topping out at in height. . The black sled dog, also known as the okteff, was native to Angalpuk.

Average temperatures in Angalpuk ranged from . In the month of Flamerule, temperatures ranged from . During the months of Eleasis through Uktar, they ranged from .
entities.short_description: Angalpuk, also called the "Eastern Basin", was one of the three regions of the Great Glacier.

entities.name: Angelhead Mine
entities.description:
Angelhead Mine was a mine found in the Sword Coast North in the late 15 century DR. It was likely named for the enormous statue of an angelic being found within its depths.

The mine lay beneath the hills just inland from Raven Cliff Beach, a short distance away from Cragmire Keep and Cragmire Barrow and just off the High Road north of Neverwinter.

The mine had several entrances standing amongst the hills. These were supported with high arches built into sturdy stone walls, with wooden pillars and a shelter out the front. Each arch was secured with a portcullis to bar entry.

Found lying amongst the rocks outside the main mine entrance was a runestone inscribed with runes of an unknown script and language. A translation read "with a heavy pick slung over his shoulder the bearded miner heads deep into the earth in search of precious metals and gemstones the quintessential dwarf".

entities.name: River Angol
entities.description:
The River Angol was a long and swift river found in the Greenfields in southern Unther.

The River Angol was formed by a network of streams on the northern Unthangol Mountains that flowed east across the Greenfields before draining into the Alamber Sea. Its waters provided sediment for the fertile lands of the Greenfields, but the river was unpredictable in its floods, much like the River Alamber.

The river disappeared after the violent changes in the southern region of Unther, that occurred because of the Spellplague of 1385 DR.

entities.name: Angry Coxswain
entities.description:
The Angry Coxswain was a tavern located in Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

The Angry Coxswain was located in the central section Waterdeep's Dock Ward along the waterfront where Odd Street joined Dock Street.

The tavern was owned by a Mulan named Ramas Shehepset in the . The house brewmaster at this time was a duergar named Orth Ironchisel.

A magical portal existed within the tavern that Ramas and Orth used to ferry slaves to Mulhorand. The portal connected directly to a prison cell located in a market in Skuld.

entities.name: Angrym's Livery
entities.description:
Angrym's Livery was a stable and horse trader in Thentia. It was owned and operated by the ranger Angrym in 1367 DR.

Angrym's was in the south-eastern corner of Thentia, fairly close to the docks.

Angrym's was fully equipped to buy and sell, as well as generally care for and house horses and rarer creatures such as griffons, pegasi, and hippogriffs. It also had the facilities to shoe animals, having its own farrier and blacksmith.

The office had a backroom that was used exclusively by passing rangers and Harpers who needed a place to conduct private business.
entities.short_description: Angrym's Livery was a stable and horse trader in Thentia. It was owned and operated by the ranger Angrym in 1367 DR.

entities.name: Angsaas Chain
entities.description:
The Angsaas, or "Eastern Shield", was a chain of mountains in the east of the Great Glacier.

The Angsaas Chain overlooked the plains of Sossal and formed the border between that land and Angalpuk. It was one of the three Saas, "Shields", that surrounded and protected the Great Glacier and divided it off from the rest of Toril.

White caribou grazed on the lower slopes of the southern mountains of the chain. As in the other Shields, remorhaz also were present here in large numbers. White dragons also laired in the tallest peaks in the southern parts.

entities.name: Anhaurz
entities.description:
Anhaurz was a city located in Lapendrar, a region of Thay, at one point, a molten ruin, and, once again, rebuilt as a fortress city in the 15 century DR.

Anhaurz was built on the southern shores of the River Lapendrar, and had a strategically important bridge across it. The town was guarding a passage across the First Escarpment.

The autharch of the city was Ramas Ankhalab. After it was rebuilt after the Spellpague, So-Kehur was assigned the restoration and stewardship of the fortress by Szass Tam.

In 1385 DR, during the Spellplague, the city was hit by azure fire, melting the city and killing its every inhabitant. By the , Anhaurz was rebuilt as a fortress city by So-Kehur, who earned for war and designed the city with that aspiration in mind. Under his rulership, the city was prided for its impressive garrison capable of withstanding any attack.

entities.description:
The Temple of Anhur was a temple dedicated to the worship of Anhur, the god of war within the Mulhorandi pantheon.

The temple was located in the the northwest corner of Skuld's Central Ward in the north section of the city.

entities.name: Tower of Anhur
entities.description:
The Tower of Anhur was a sacred tower located in the capital city of Skuld in Mulhorand during the mid–14 century DR.

The Tower was located in the southwest corner of the City of the Gods in the northcentral part of the city.

As its name implied, the Tower of Anhur was once the home of an incarnation of Anhur who held the title of God-King in Mulhorand. It was constructed by slaves thousands of years ago as of the .

entities.description:
The Animal Handlers' Affiliation was the guildhall for ranchers, drovers and veterinary physicians in the city of Daggerford in the Western Heartlands in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

The guildhall was located in the northwest section of Daggerford on Fields Lane near the Farmer's Gate.

entities.name: Anjiro
entities.description:
Anjiro was a village in Aru Province on the island of Tsukishima in Wa, lying near the capital town of Aru.

In , the headman of Anjiro grew suspicious of events in the village and wrote a report to the daimyo of the province, Benju Matsutomo. Although Benju asked for more details, the headman fell out of contact. Then, in the summer of that year, his body was discovered dead in the House of Heavenly Sand in Aru, having been poisoned and dumped there by ninja, likely the Yamaguchi clan that served Eichiro Tanaka of Anjiro.

entities.name: Ankaram
entities.description:
Duchy Ankaram, formerly Ankramir, was the territory of Tethyr bordering Calimshan in the south.

Ankaram was located between the River Ith and the River Memnon. It was bordered by the Sea of Swords in the west and the Forest of Mir in the east.

The region was sparsely populated but included several well-guarded forts along the border, so Calimshan was cautious about ever attacking it.

The duchy contained two counties, Calimmon and Monteshi, the latter of which included Monrativi Teshy Mir, an area of contention between Calimshan and Tethyr.
entities.short_description: Duchy Ankaram, formerly Ankramir, was the territory of Tethyr bordering Calimshan in the south.

entities.name: Ankhapur
entities.description:
Ankhapur was a city located in the Lake of Steam region on the southern edge of interior Faerûn.

The city was primarily known for its pearl industry, which involved many of its citizens.

There were a number of tressym in the city. Curiously, on the day before Highsummer each year, every tressym in the city mysteriously disappeared only to return three days later.

Ankhapur was originally settled as a military outpost of the Jhaamdath Empire around -5000DR, and is the only such city along the Lake of Steams northern coastline to have remained continuously settled throughout the ages. Unlike all other cities along the Arnaden, Ankhapur alone was not completely resettled by Calishites, having retained their Jhaamdathan roots and appearing more like a city of the Vilhon Reach or Tethyr. In 1366 DR, Manferic III ruled Ankhapur with an iron hand and a touch of sadism. He became a lich and sought to inhabit the body of Janol Famisso, a bastard son of his. In his attempt, Manferic killed his other heirs while controlling Janol's body in order to inherit the throne from himself. However, thanks to a cleric of Lathander, Lissa, and others, Manferic was destroyed by Janol and his allies.

entities.description:
The River Ankhapur was a small waterway found near the Lake of Steam.

The river originated near the center of the Ankhwood north of the eastern half of the Lake of Steam. It flowed southwest and west for before emptying into the sea approximately southeast of Ankhapur.

entities.description:
Ankhwood (once part of the Winterwood) was a forest whose insect, animal and plant populations become mutated. There were once wild magic and dead magic areas orbiting one another in the forest, but by 1374 DR this effect had subsided and the elves living in the area were investigating the cause of the mutations.

entities.name: Ankhwugaht
entities.description:
Ankhwugaht was the divine realm of Set, the Pharaonic and Mulhorandi god of evil.

Set actually maintained more than one version of Ankhwugaht. His home realm was the version in Stygia, but there was also the relatively smaller "Ankhwugaht Prime" or "Little Ankhwugaht" in Avernus, and others like it.

Ankhwugaht was a desert realm of poisoned sands, a place of the scorpion's sting and the viper's kiss. Many things might differ between its specific incarnations, but a constant was the prostration before the power of almighty Set.

Ankhwugaht empowered and extended all necromancy spells, although in the Great Wheel cosmology this effect only applied to those used for evil purposes.
entities.short_description: Ankhwugaht was the divine realm of Set, the Pharaonic and Mulhorandi god of evil.

entities.name: Ankle Bells
entities.description:
Ankle Bells was a busy and expensive tavern in Tharkar of the Free Cities of Parsanic, and the second-most-crowded space after Donder's Dancing Masques.

The tavern had a damp and spacious cellar that held a hidden smugglers' tunnel that led to the harbor of Tharkar. The upper floors of the building were used as guest rooms for their many clients.

The guest rooms in Ankle Bells were famously scented and perfumed to hide other unpalatable human odors.

The Bells, like many other public places in the city, had a strong dislike for the dangerous Daggers of Tharkar and had a contingency plan in case one of the clients needed to escape. The tavern had a false trapped door to distract the possible Daggers' intrusion, as well as another one that collapsed if forced open, among quite a few others.
entities.short_description: Ankle Bells was a busy and expensive tavern in Tharkar of the Free Cities of Parsanic, and the second-most-crowded space after Donder's Dancing Masques.

entities.name: Anklis Island
entities.description:
Anklis Island was a small island in the Crowded Sea within west Zakhara.

Anklis Island was the northernmost island of the archipelago of Al-Zulm Islands. The island was located just south of Durrar Island and the Pearl Banks. Much of the coast of Anklis Island was rocky, while scattered grasslands and deserts could be found in its interior. The entire island was surrounded by coral reefs and submerged rocks sat offshore of the southwest coast. A smaller unnamed island sat off the southeast shore. The island measured roughly wide and long. There were no settlements on Anklis Island as of 1367 DR.

entities.name: Ankramir
entities.description:
The Principality of Ankramir was the southwestern principality of Tethyr.

Ankramir included the duchies of Kamlann, the Purple Marches, and Ankaram, and was the location of Tethyr's former capital and largest city, Zazesspur.

The region was sparsely populated, relative to other areas of Tethyr. In cultural feel, it was akin to Calimshan, which bordered it to the south.

Formally, this principality was under the authority of Princess Cyriana Rhindaun in 1370 DR, who was the daughter of Queen Zaranda Star Rhindaun and her consort King Haedrak Rhindaun III. Since the princess was a young child at that time, the ruling of the principality was handled by Cyriana's regent, Vajra Valmeyjar, the Duchess of Ankaram.
entities.short_description: The Principality of Ankramir was the southwestern principality of Tethyr.

entities.name: Anok-Imaskar
entities.description:
Anok-Imaskar was an empire that existed in ancient Kara-Tur, under the reign of Emperor Kujawa. It was one of the three successor states of the Imaskar Empire after it fell in , the others being Deep Imaskar

Unlike Imaskar's vassals, Durpar and Gundavar, which descended into barbarism, and the Raurin, which became a desert wasteland, the eastern provinces of Imaskar emerged relatively unscathed from the destruction of the western empire. The mountainous Khati province and the flatter Katakoro province). With that, he declared himself Emperor and founded a new realm, Anok-Imaskar.

Anok-Imaskar was prosperous and quickly spread east, north, and south across Kara-Tur. Many great magical scrolls and artifacts were traded from Tempat Larang to the empire during his reign. However, the southern empire was harassed by the Segara Sea Lords, powerful and far-ranging pirates of the Segara Sea. When Sangkal Chunbi, governor of Tempat Larang, issued warrants for their arrest, the pirate leader Chan Chiong tried to cut Tempat Larang off from the empire by seizing Sampar, the empire's only southern harbor. However, the canny Chunbi defeated Chan Chiong through a ruse and rehired the pirates, transforming them into a southern fleet for the empire.

Unfortunately, the nearby volcano Mount Bakos erupted in , covering Tempat Larang in ash and lava and in poisonous gases that slew the citizens. Over the following decades, the empire's southwestern lands were also abandoned. According to later accounts, the emperor thought this disaster was an omen from the gods, and hence abandoned his plans for the south, even erasing them from official records. Thus only vague legends of Tempat Larang survived.
entities.short_description: Anok-Imaskar was an empire that existed in ancient Kara-Tur, under the reign of Emperor Kujawa. It was one of the three successor states of the Imaskar Empire after it fell in , the others being Deep Imaskar

entities.name: Ansi
entities.description:
Ansi , meaning West Protecting Fortress, was a small town located in the northern regions of the Quoya Desert within the Hordelands around 1359 DR.

The small town of Ansi was little more than a fortified inn built near an oasis of bitter water.

What little importance the town had came from the fact that it sat at the top of a narrow pass in the hills of the Quoya Desert, and only its close proximity to Shou Lung kept it from being totally unknown.

The town itself was mostly rundown buildings, surrounded by a wall of brick. The wells produced enough water for a few small melon farms, but farming in the area was difficult because of the constant winds blowing dust, which often accumulated along the walls, sometimes even spilling over.

entities.name: Ansildabar's Last Rest
entities.description:
Ansildabar's Last Rest was a crypt in Hastarl, Athalantar, during the 3 century DR.

The tomb was in a walled-off burial ground across the city from the Wanton Wench, a tavern.

The crypt had a sloping roof, which was shaded by two trees. The burial ground was largely in disrepair, with trees growing through some of the buildings.

Other than being walled off, the burial ground was left completely unguarded.
entities.short_description: Ansildabar's Last Rest was a crypt in Hastarl, Athalantar, during the 3 century DR.

entities.name: Ansong
entities.description:
Ansong was a settlement in the kingdom of Koryo in Kara-Tur.

Ansong lay on the eastern coast, facing the Straits of Koryo.

The shipwrights of Ansong built the very best ships in the land. Some were created with magic that enabled them to float more easily and to sail more swiftly, such that seemed to fly over and above the waves when at full sail. They also built barges that never rocked in heavy seas. Thus, foreigners from Wa and as far as Shou Lung came to Ansong to purchase ships.

The fishermen of Ansong, along with those of In'ani, were claimed to be the best in the world, having done such things as eliminate the prides of sea lions in the Straits of Koryo and catch the enormous eel Ghartii Nung.

entities.description:
Anteos Lane was a street of hard-packed dirt and gravel in the North Ward of Waterdeep.

This street ran from east to west, coming southwest off of Trollkill Street and curving eastward. It eventually turned northeast and terminated into Brassfeather Lane.

entities.name: Anteos Villa
entities.description:
Anteos Villa was the family estate of the Waterdhavian noble house Anteos.

The Anteos Villa was located in the North Ward of Waterdeep, on the corner of Anteos Lane and Trollkill Street. It stood across from the Phull Villa.

Like many Waterdhavian villas in the North Ward, this was a walled estate featuring a landscaped garden with elaborate adornments. Inside the walls of the estate were two high-quality buildings that stood two stories and one story tall, these being the mansion proper and a guesthouse respectively.

In the , Lord Hamar Anteos had an affair with Kyara Ruldegost, a young Tethyrian woman distantly related to the Ruldegost clan. The lord of that clan at the time, the ill-tempered Econ Ruldegost, was incensed by the matter that he engaged Hamar in a duel and lost his life. With his dying breath he laid a curse upon House Anteos, proclaiming that they would be, "...heirless until they recognize and accept the ruin they have done me and mine."

entities.name: Anthather's Mill
entities.description:
Anthather's Mill was a water mill somewhere in Faerûn.

Anthather's Mill stood over a fork in the road. The land around it was largely farmlands, broken up by large stones.

The building was made of fieldstone, and had a pool where the stream that turned its wheel was dammed. The pool continued along one of the roads.

A Chosen of Mystra, Elminster Aumar, asked for directions at Anthather's Mill when looking for the Riven Stone, learning it was just down the road from there.
entities.short_description: Anthather's Mill was a water mill somewhere in Faerûn.

entities.name: Antholo's All the Realms
entities.description:
Antholo's All the Realms was a map and chart shop in Delzimmer, southeast Faerûn, owned by Antholo Kraul circa the .

Antholo's was located on Riuntle Street in Delzimmer, a crossroads town (before the ) located between the Great Rift, the Eastern Shaar, Luiren, and the Forest of Amtar.

The shop was an unremarkable store front among many on Riuntle Street.

The maps and charts at Antholo's sold for 25 to 200 gold pieces. The more expensive ones were larger, newer, and/or in demand, but all were much more practical than decorative—showing the essential elements without much cluttering detail. Examples of his wares included copies of trade charts from Calimshan, Tharsult, and the Tashalar, which were themselves mostly copied from more authoritative originals kept in monasteries, royal libraries, and Candlekeep.
entities.short_description: Antholo's All the Realms was a map and chart shop in Delzimmer, southeast Faerûn, owned by Antholo Kraul circa the .

entities.name: Anthormbrur
entities.description:
Anthormbrur was the name of the klathlaaedin (ornately carved stone mansion) belonging to the elite Horthander family located in Khôltar, south Faerûn circa the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR.

This elegant compound was located on the northeast side of Hael Way on the point of land between Hael Way and the North Way. It backed up against Baharrokhbrur, the klathlaaedin belonging to the rival Khaundrove family, which faced North Way to the east.

The eye-catching feature of this klathlaaedin was the central five-story needle-tower with its outer surface covered with leaping flames, human faces with watchful eyes, and many beasts, both mundane and monstrous, all carved into the stone. A squat, two-story attachment with a large, round window facing the courtyard connected the tower with the two wings. Both wings were sturdy three-floor rectangular buildings with sharply peaked roofs that formed a wide angle embracing the courtyard and gardens. The once-extensive enclosed gardens were mostly converted to stables as the Horthander passion for racing horses grew.

entities.name: Antoumek
entities.description:
Antoumek was a small town located along the shores of the Lake of Mists in the Hordelands in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Antoumek sat along the southern shore of the Lake of Mists in between Almorel to the east and Strelsi to the west. It was located approximately north of the Golden Way.

entities.name: Anvil
entities.description:
Anvil was a neighborhood of Ravens Bluff's Crow's End district and the very epicenter of activity surrounding the city's inner harbor, Clearwater Harbor, due in large part to being where the government's central customs office was located. Any goods brought into the city with the intent of staying had to go through here for inspection, packing, and labeling. This made Anvil the veritable "heart and soul" of the economic business that kept Ravens Bluff alive, as well as a neighborhood where every criminal group, shipping concern, and merchant house desired to have a presence and influence over.

The name of the neighborhood was popularly associated with a Ravenian saying that dated back to the days of Sarbreen. It was said to be the place "where the hammer comes down", with some saying so with an unspoken implication that the phrase continued on as, "and only the strong survive."

Anvil was composed of around twenty-two or so city blocks and hosted five docks. At its eastern end the neighborhood butted the DeVillars Creek, until terminating along Omphrel's Span, the creek's most downstream bridge. From the west it was bordered by the neighborhood of Bitterstone, which it shared nine streets with, with Blacktree Boulevard South running along their boundary line. To the north it was bordered by Altarside, which it shared seven streets with, with Morlgar's Ride running along their boundary line.

Anvil's buildings sported the most architectural variety out of anywhere in the city. And nowhere else could one find as profuse a collection of people of different races, backgrounds, and social classes rubbing shoulders. Anvil was also popular amongst most adventurers as a place to find drink and company.

entities.name: Apanu
entities.description:
Apanu was a stone-built fortress in the Kuong Kingdom in Malatra, standing just south of the northern border with T'u Lung.

The fortress was built as a show of strength, but T'u Lung displayed little interest in marching over the border. Circa 1357 DR, it had a garrison of 1,000 soldiers, who conducted patrols of the surrounding jungle and provided escorts for the merchant caravans.

entities.name: Aphonion
entities.description:
Aphonion was a world on the Prime Material plane protected by a powerful Magi member of the Order of the Eternals and the home of some unique spells. Some of the lands of note on Aphonion included the Kingdom of Stream's End.

In the late 14 century DR, the Order of the Eternals, a trans-dimensional guild for magic-users of impressive power, elected to hold its 1,238 annual Symposium in the city of Ravens Bluff on the world of Toril, in order to secretly investigate its unusually high levels of magical energies and planar incursions. The Symposium's attendees included Magi Paragon the Purple, one of the High Masters of the Order, and Lady Dowager Duchess Darra de Aerindale. All the guests stayed at Glittering Star Inn for the multi-day event. Paragon the Purple, however, was a victim of an opportunistic robbery with his cloak of the art and spellbook taken, and eventually returned with some aid from the wizardly heroes of the Living City. During the Symposium, Paragon the Purple helmed the opening lecture titled Necromancy: The Blackest Art.

entities.name: Aphrunn Mountains
entities.description:
The Aphrunn Mountains were a mountain range forming the southern border of the republic of Turmish in the Vilhon Reach. The mountains were visible from the island of Ilighôn on the other side of the Farshore Straits. Lilit Pass allowed passage through the Aphrunn, connecting Turmish to the Vilhon.

The gold dragon Frizzerfraz made his home in these mountains. A tribe of kobolds called the Scything Claw resided and in the Aphrunn and would occasionally raid into Turmish.

There was an active volcano in the Aphrunn mountains called Mount Kolimnis. In the wizard Danirro of Alaghôn, on the behalf of the nearby city of Gildenglade attempted to quell the volcano through the use of magic. While he was in the process of casting a spell on the volcano, however, he was murdered by agents of the Emerald Enclave who threw him into Mount Kolimnis. The Enclave then destroyed all remains of Danirro's research, warning others to not interfere with the volcano or other forces they did not understand.

The volcano erupted and destroyed Gildenglade in 1423 DR.

entities.name: Apothec
entities.description:
Apothec was an ancient Netherese realm that prospered for a time until it was destroyed by the plagues of Moander.

The realm lay in southeast Netheril near the Desertsmouth Mountains, along the Pox River which flowed from Moander's Footstep.

The Apothecs shared a common ancestry with the Netherese people, but eschewed the use of magic in favor of herbalism, medicine, and other more natural cures for ailments. They enjoyed good relations with the Netherese, and heavily traded with each other.

In , Moander tainted the Pox River with a lethal and virulent plague. The Apothecs were unable to resist it, and they were completely wiped out. Though they ceased to exist, the term "apothecary" came to be commonly used in the Realms for all those who made medicines and cures.
entities.short_description: Apothec was an ancient Netherese realm that prospered for a time until it was destroyed by the plagues of Moander.

entities.name: Apothecary
entities.description:
The apothecary in Triboar was a shop belonging to Tarmock Felaskur that sold medicine as of the late 15 century DR. It was also notable for its carbonated sweet water.

The shop was located on the east side of town north of the Evermoor Way. It sat across the street from the Northshield House inn.

The building was a sunken wood cottage covered in ivy and marked by a wooden sign in the shape of a potion bottle. A broken wheelbarrow sat out front just beneath the sign.

The store sold herbal remedies and salves of dubious effectiveness. It also sold sweet water for 1 gold piece per flask.
entities.short_description: The apothecary in Triboar was a shop belonging to Tarmock Felaskur that sold medicine as of the late 15 century DR. It was also notable for its carbonated sweet water.

entities.name: The Apple Tree Inn
entities.description:
The Apple Tree Inn was a ryokan (inn) in Aru in Wa in the 1770s on the Wa Calendar. Small and unremarkable, it stood in the Pilgrim District, near the gate to the Shining Temple of Bishamon, and was likely named for the temple's sacred apple tree.

The thief Komatsu stayed at The Apple Tree Inn in , and might've been confronted by adventurers there.

entities.name: Appointments with the Mighty
entities.description:
Appointments with the Mighty was a shop located in Huzuz in 1367 DR.

Appointments with the Mighty could be found in the Pilgrims' District of the City of Delights.

Rayad al-Farif owned and operated this establishment.

Rayad claimed to be able to make appointments for his customers with the heads of the various mosques or even the Grand Caliph. He only charged his customers if he succeeded in making the appointment.
entities.short_description: Appointments with the Mighty was a shop located in Huzuz in 1367 DR.

entities.name: Apprentice Row
entities.description:
Apprentice Row was an area in the city of Neverwinter prior to the mid–15 century DR.

Apprentice Row was located in or adjacent to the Arcanist Quarter in the southeastern portion of the city.

Before the eruption of Mount Hotenow in the , the large number of powerful wizards and other spellcasters who congregated at the Arcanist Quarter led the area to become attractive to those who wished to learn from them. The result was a neighborhood of rundown apartments and cheap taverns catering to these aspiring mages.

A motley mix of would-be mages from all social classes rubbed elbows in the tenements and taverns of Apprentice Row. These young spellcasters worked tirelessly to hone their craft and attract the attention of a powerful master to take them on as apprentice.
entities.short_description: Apprentice Row was an area in the city of Neverwinter prior to the mid–15 century DR.

entities.name: Aquas and Azures
entities.description:
Aquas and Azures was an exclusive jeweler's and gemcutter's shop in Calimport specializing in blue-colored gems around 1370 DR.

The store was located in Mayya Drudach of Najja Sabban in Wizard Ward.

Aquas and Azures was a seven-story minaret tower with no entrance at either the ground level or from the drudach or sabban wall paths. Instead, the only entrance was high up on the open balcony near the top of the tower. Thus, flying was the only way to enter the shop, and walls of force kept anyone uninvited out (though they did not trap customers in.)

One was only allowed to peruse the collection of sapphires and other blue gemstones by invitation only. If of high enough social status, a potential customer would be delivered an appointment form. At the time of the appointment, a blue flying carpet would be sent down to carry the client up to the balcony to enter the store.
entities.short_description: Aquas and Azures was an exclusive jeweler's and gemcutter's shop in Calimport specializing in blue-colored gems around 1370 DR.

entities.name: Aqueduct of Axalt
entities.description:
The Aqueduct of Axalt was a wonder of engineering and a famous landmark that rose above the Valley of Nexal in Maztica.

The Aqueduct began at the freshwater pool formed by the lush Cicada Spring that ran off Mount Popol's southwestern slope. The waster was carried by the Aqueduct of Axalt for over eight miles, to the north, over the great Lake of Tezca and ended in a reservoir at the Sacred Plaza of Nexal.

The Aqueduct of Axalt was a wide structure with two troughs, allowing the water supply never to stop even when the aqueduct was cleaned or repaired.

The aqueduct that supplied Nexal with freshwater was built during the twenty-two-year reign of the Revered Counsellor Axalt, the successor of Chalco. It was considered to be the most impressive accomplishment of the Revered Counsellor of Nexal and greatly benefited the city, bringing fresh, clean, and good-tasting spring water made available to all. Despite the fact that the four great lakes that surrounded Nexal city had drinkable water, the Aqueduct of Axalt provided water of better quality.
entities.short_description: The Aqueduct of Axalt was a wonder of engineering and a famous landmark that rose above the Valley of Nexal in Maztica.

entities.name: Aquessir
entities.description:
Aquessir, also known as Shadowtop Borough, was a floating city of Netheril. Noted for its inhabitants' friendly disposition towards outsiders, as well as being the original home of the malevolent Crown of Horns, Aquessir was destroyed in when the city's mythallar failed.

Aquessir was most commonly found floating near Shadowtop Alp, which overlooked the Janick river.

Unlike most other Netherese enclaves, the inhabitants of Aquessir were happy to participate in trade with outsiders, particularly elves. Although Aquessir was home to many arcane researchers, the creation of quasi-magical items was never popular within the enclave.

The city was founded by the archwizard Trebbe in . Trebbe ruled Aquessir until he died in while finishing his work on the artifact known as the Crown of Horns. The ensuing explosion leveled an entire city block, and the artifact was subsequently lost.

entities.name: Arabel
entities.description:
Arabel () was a fortified city in northern Cormyr. The city stood at an important crossroads and was a major trade center.

A person from Arabel was known as an Arabellan.

Arabel was at the junction of the High Road, Calantar's Way, the East Way, and the Moonsea Ride. The farming town of Clarkswell was located fifty miles north of Arabel, in the foothills of the Storm Horn Mountains.

The city contained almost a thousand structures in 1357 DR.

entities.name: Arabellan Palace
entities.description:
The Arabellan Palace was the home of the ruler of Arabel in Cormyr.

The palace was luxurious to behold. It had five narrow towers, with elegantly sweeping turrets and conical roofs. The palace contained the court of Myrmeen Lhal and an assembly hall.

The palace was located in the most prosperous section of the city, the north, being surrounded by the citadel and multiple mansions of the rich elite and by the Lady's House, a temple to Tymora.

Soldiers of the Purple Dragons were stationed as palace guards. These were members of the city's garrison, which was under the command of Myrmeen Lhal.
entities.short_description: The Arabellan Palace was the home of the ruler of Arabel in Cormyr.

entities.name: Arach-Tinilith
entities.description:
Arach-Tinilith was the clerical school in the drow city of Menzoberranzan. Like the rest of the Academy, it was located in Tier Breche.

The complex -- the largest of the Academy -- was located on the northern side of the Tier Breche cavern and was shaped like a spider. The "cephalothorax" of the spider housed the grandest chapels, the holiest altars, and the quarters of the senior priestesses. The crowning gem of the complex was the main chapel, carved from a single mass of black stone. Inside, seats surrounded a circular platform that held a statue of a spider with the head of a drow female.

The Mistress of the academy had an office on the highest level that had a tapestry depicting Lolth looming over a sacrificed surface elf.

There were dungeon-like kitchens located in the lower levels. Slaves, such as the ogre slave Chirank in 1361 DR, were employed there.
entities.short_description: Arach-Tinilith was the clerical school in the drow city of Menzoberranzan. Like the rest of the Academy, it was located in Tier Breche.

entities.description:
Araksa was a small island located off of the eastern coast of Evermeet on the Trackless Sea.

Araksa sat roughly due east of the coastal town of Taltempla, or northeast of the island of Sumbrar.

Of the satellite islands surrounding the elven homeland of Evermeet, Araksa was by far the smallest.

entities.name: Aralent
entities.description:
Aralent was a settlement in the Deepwing Mountains in the Vilhon Reach.

It was the site of the House of the Harmed temple of Ilmater, and home to the well-respected priest Master Sufferer Olbedan.

In the Year of the Boot, 1343 DR, the people of Hlondeth in the Vilhon Reach requested that the Graycloak's Wolves adventuring company deliver the Tome of Torment—the holiest book of the church of Ilmater—to Master Sufferer Olbedan at the House of the Harmed in Aralent. However, during the harsh winter, Graycloak's Wolves fell prey to doppelgangers and leucrotta preying on travellers and never made it to Olbedan. The Tome was thought lost in the winter snows.

entities.name: Arambar Gulch
entities.description:
Arambar Gulch was a canyon located in Laerakond, related somehow to the primordial Arambar.

During the dragonborn rebellion, one of the major battles was fought at Arambar Gulch.

Category:Locations in Laerakond Category:Locations on Abeir Category:Locations

entities.name: Arandron
entities.description:
Arandron was a continent a long distance to the southwest of Faerûn.

Around the 8 century DR, there was a bustling port city on Arandron called Haunvaerune, inhabited by humans. Ships such as Captain Imbryn Ultal's Aelusteen sailed between Haunvaerune and Lantan to trade in Lantanna inventions.

Behind the city was a high, bare rocky ridge upon which stood Steelspires, a castle constructed by stone giants for the steel dragons Malavauvrantarandra and Phaudrantanthildrar.

Ed Greenwood mentions "the continent of Arandron far to the southwest of Faerûn", but its exact position is unknown and there are three candidates on the map of Toril. The continent of Katashaka also lies southwest of Faerûn, and is identified as the largest of the southwestern continents, labeled "Unknown Lands". This article presumes Arandron to be the unlabeled continent lying below Faerûn and between the two labeled "Unknown Lands". Regardless, Arandron may be another name for Katashaka.
entities.short_description: Arandron was a continent a long distance to the southwest of Faerûn.

entities.name: Aranghthal
entities.description:
Aranghthal was a dragonborn settlement in Relmaur, Laerakond.

Aranghthal was one of the two "mobile" settlements the Relmorn dragonborn always maintained near the city of Rokthorl. Every time the location of Rokthorl changed, the dragonborn also moved Aranghthal to a western cavern near the capital's current location.

entities.name: Araugul
entities.description:
Araugul (}}) was the great fortress-city capital of Hlundadim in the Goblin Marches and later Anauroch.

At the time of its founding, Araugul lay in the Windy Plains region of the southern Netheril steppes, midway between the Shinantra Mountains and the Storm Horns, not far southeast of the cities of Kismet and Rasilith. As the Anauroch desert expanded past it, it came be in the Sword between the Quarter of Emptiness to the north and the habitable remains of the Goblin Marches to the south.

The southern frontier of Netheril had long been fought over by tribes of goblinoids, orcs, and other humanoids, with the goblins becoming the most powerful and entrenched group by the Shadowed Age. The arrival of the mysterious Great Hlundadim in the , led to the creation of the nation of Hlundadim and the great fortress of Araugul in the Windy Plains, unifying many disparate groups into an army with a single identity.

Dust storms and the desertification of the Windy Plains by 268 DR drove the inhabitants of Araugul into a panic, sending them fleeing south as the land seemed to turn against them. The Great Hlundadim disappeared as well, and the nation of Hlundadim ceased to exist. Over the following centuries Araugul and the lands around it were slowly resettled as the goblinoids and their kin attempted to rebuild what was lost.
entities.short_description: Araugul (}}) was the great fortress-city capital of Hlundadim in the Goblin Marches and later Anauroch.

entities.name: Araumycos
entities.description:
Araumycos (, Dwarvish for "Great Fungus") was an enormous fungal growth that lived in the Upper Northdark of the Underdark, and lay beneath the High Forest between the cities of Menzoberranzan and Ched Nasad.

Araumycos was a huge life form, a single organism that covered almost all the parts of the Underdark beneath the High Forest, beginning at a depth of 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) under the surface and ending at a depth of 3 miles (4.8 kilometers). It was believed to extend from the Shining Falls to the Lost Peaks and from Tall Trees to the Hall of Four Ghosts, wholly occupying the labyrinth of tunnels and caverns that existed beneath the High Forest. But it seemed that it had reached its peak of volume since it no longer grew through other territories by 1372 DR.

It was described as spongy, grey, and humid, similar to the outside of a brain.

The area where Araumycos was located was once mined and occupied by the dwarves of Ammarindar, during the time of the elf realm Eaerlann.

entities.name: Araundordoom
entities.description:
Araundordoom was a rather typical doom in the Underdark of Faerûn controlled by the once-human lich Araundor.

Like most lich dooms, Araundordoom was a labyrinthine network of twisted tunnels and cave rooms, with hiding places for magic items.

Araundor filled pools of water in his doom with poison and snare traps to grab intruders' legs. He would hide underwater in such pools or in pools of mud through which they could also be trapped. Araundor avoided placing crushing traps, because liches were not immune to being physically smashed.

Araundor discovered the passageways and rooms that he claimed as his doom.
entities.short_description: Araundordoom was a rather typical doom in the Underdark of Faerûn controlled by the once-human lich Araundor.

entities.name: Arbalest's House
entities.description:
The Arbalest's House was a monastery and the most significant temple to Milil circa 1358 DR.

Arbalest's House was located on a hilltop in the town of Athkatla, north of Goldspires and of the harbor.

The walls, floors and ceilings of the temple were mostly made of stone. Its most notable architectural feature was the Bellows of Milil, a gigantic pipe organ intertwined with the structure of building itself.

The Bellows of Milil provided the temple with several protecting spells, with both defensive and offensive capabilities. It also contained several caches in the form of false pipes, used to store most of the temple's treasure (perfectly formed gemstones).
entities.short_description: The Arbalest's House was a monastery and the most significant temple to Milil circa 1358 DR.

entities.name: Arblood Street
entities.description:
Arblood Street was a road found within Tulmon along the Lake of Steam during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Dashalam Winery, a winery specializing in ruby wine and sherry, was located along Arblood Street.

entities.name: Arbonne
entities.description:
Arbonne was a tiny fishing village in the Vast in the mid-to-late 14 century DR.{{cite web

It lay on the shore of the Sea of Fallen Stars, somewhere south of Procampur.

Apart from a few outlying farms, Arbonne made its living off the sea. It had its own shipbuilder, known as Justin of Arbonne.

entities.name: Arbor Square
entities.description:
Arbor Square was a large public plaza roughly at the center of Halarahh in the wizard nation of Halruaa.

Arbor Square stood at the center of the loop formed by the Promenade. To the west from it stood the grand Zalathorm's Palace and immediately to the south – the Dockside Square.

The plaza was a beautiful and spacious square built out of green and pink stone. The plaza was decorated with intricate pink grape vine-shaded iron trellises and arches. Numerous chairs, benches, and small tables were placed all around the Arbor Square, offering passers-by rest in the shade of the hot southern sun. The air around the square was filled with sweet fragrances of grapes, overripe oranges, and savory aromas of the open-air market, mixed with the fresh smell of the Great Sea.

The center of the Arbor Square held a stage, a risen platform, used by self-absorbed orators, town criers, and musicians, as well as occasional display of wizardly magic.
entities.short_description: Arbor Square was a large public plaza roughly at the center of Halarahh in the wizard nation of Halruaa.

entities.name: Arcane Chambers
entities.description:
The Arcane Chambers made up the second level of Undermountain. It used to serve as a laboratory for Halaster Blackcloak's apprentices, and was thus infested with sentient magical experiments and other leftovers.

;Hall of the Black Helm:The Hall of the Black Helm was a 80-feet (24 meters) high dark room. It was once decorated with tapestries of armored pegasi-riders hunting dragons. It was also the destination of a gate in a room from the Dungeon Level.

;Helmwatch:People who passed the Ghost Gate entered the center of the Helmwatch-room.

;Lord Hund's Tomb:Lord Hund's Tomb was not a single room, but an entire complex that was not created by Halaster, but by people hired by Lord Hund Hiilgauntlet, a necromancer who eventually became a mummy.
entities.short_description: The Arcane Chambers made up the second level of Undermountain. It used to serve as a laboratory for Halaster Blackcloak's apprentices, and was thus infested with sentient magical experiments and other leftovers.

entities.name: Arcane Tower
entities.description:
The Arcane Tower, also referred to as the Enchanted Tower or simply the Ruined Tower, was an underground magical research site that served as the home of the Mystran cleric Lenore De Hurst for a time during the late 15 century DR. The structure exemplified an unconventional blend of technology and arcane craftsmanship, demonstrating how the dual disciplines could best be utilized for the comfort of those required to work in less-desirable circumstances.

The tower was situated in an area of the Underdark, roughly beneath the Sunlit Wetlands of the Western Heartlands. It was built overlooking the Ebonlake near a colony of myconids.

The Arcane Tower was unlike others of its kind constructed above ground. Its structure was built from stone in a fairly unremarkable architectural style, but utilized technological features and artificer seldom seen elsewhere in the Realms. Metal piping wound around and within and around the tower's exterior, conducting streams of arcane energy from a central power source at its bottommost level.

The primary entranceway and entrance chamber was found on the tower's fourth floor. While its stately appearance featured beauteous decorations it was rather cold and impersonal, and held no remarkable features. The only items of note on this level were the two arcane cannons that stood sentry over the double doors of the entrance.

entities.name: Arcanum of Magic
entities.description:
The Arcanum of Magic, also known as the Great University, was a prominent university and temple dedicated to Thoth, a common combination among Thothian temples.

The Arcanum was located in the northern part of Gheldaneth, adjacent to a wizard's college available only to Thoth's clergy.

The Arcanum was the largest building in all of Gheldaneth,

This university taught students of various ages how to count, read, and write. It also taught basic information on the Mulhorandi pantheon and the history of Mulhorand.
entities.short_description: The Arcanum of Magic, also known as the Great University, was a prominent university and temple dedicated to Thoth, a common combination among Thothian temples.

entities.name: Arcata
entities.description:
The Duchy of Arcata was a province in the Kingdom of Damara in the Cold Lands.

Arcata was the westernmost province of Damara, abutting the Galena Mountains. The land was flat and dusty.

As of 1359 DR, it was ruled by Duke William Horgath from its capital town of Valls.

Arcata traded with the other Damaran provinces via the King's Road. As one of the so-called "supply provinces," its farms produced food for the kingdom and its mines harvested iron and silver.

entities.name: Arch Hold
entities.description:
Arch Hold was a stronghold in Archendale that was a part of White Ford's defensive system.

Arch Hold was named for its strategic position, overseeing the dark and perilous Arch Wood.

It stood close to the western edge of Arch Wood and bordered White Ford's Wolfwall.

Arch Hold comprised a ring-shaped stone wall with a protective ditch. It had a dug-out sleeping quarters for the members of the one or two Rides (sixty members each) garrisoned in White Ford and the Archenriders patrolling Archendale.

entities.name: Arch of Goolgog
entities.description:
The Arch of Goolgog was an orc-made monumental arch in the Vast. It held a portal to the Battle of Bones in the Western Heartlands.

The arch was constructed on the orders of the orc leader Goolgog Elvenbane to celebrate his great victory against elves and humans in ancient times. To that end, it was fashioned from the bones of the defeated enemies on the battlefield. Goolgog marched his whole army under the arch to demonstrate his triumph, before he returned to his base.

In the late 11th century DR (shortly after circa 1072 DR), followers of the god of the dead, Myrkul, Lord of Bones, arrived at the Arch of Goolgog. They built a hidden temple close by, and desired a swift means of joining their brethren near the Well of Dragons in the Battle of Bones. One of their number was a sorcerer, and they worked together to create a portal within the arch and linked it to the center of the Battle of the Bones valley. The priests also animated the bones of the arch to defend it against the unfaithful.

Eventually, however, the temple to Myrkul was destroyed (well before 1358 DR), and the priesthood scattered and took up with other gods. The clergy as a whole forgot about the portal, as well as the passphrase for it. In addition, the Cult of the Dragon attacked and pillaged the Myrkulyte temple near the Well of Dragons too, around 1312 DR, so all knowledge of the portal there was also lost.
entities.short_description: The Arch of Goolgog was an orc-made monumental arch in the Vast. It held a portal to the Battle of Bones in the Western Heartlands.

entities.name: Arch Wood
entities.description:
Arch Wood was a tiny village hidden inside the forest of Arch Wood in the Dalelands and largely unknown to the outside world.

The village consisted of a small cluster of cottages, a blacksmith, and a watermill.

The Selûnite priestess and werewolf Feena Archwood lived in Arch Wood in the mid-to-late 14 century DR, both fighting a protracted war against Malarite lycanthropes and serving the community as a healer. She was preceded by her mother, Maleva, also a priest of Selûne who fought against Malarites.

entities.name: Archenbridge
entities.description:
Archenbridge was the only major town of Archendale, and its de facto capital. as well as one of their most important trading hubs.

Archenbridge was located along the River Arkhen, at the mouth of the Arkhen Vale.

Its proximity to the Sembian border caused Archenbridge to be the first stop of many caravanners.

As a result Archenbridge enjoyed a vibrant economy revolving around markets and merchant houses, the center of the town being as busy as Waterdeep at any hour of the day. Its markets were amongst the largest of the Dales, and its merchants amongst the richest.

The Archenbridge sewers were a sanitation system of tunnels beneath the small city of Archenbridge in Archendale.

These sewers were directly connected to the River Arkhen, which carried away its waste.

entities.name: Archendale
entities.description:
Archendale (}}), one of the lands' trading Dales, was the most aggressive, influential and well-defended of the dales within the Dalelands. The large trading hub viewed themselves as the leader of the region, boasting the largest standing army and strong economy based on its self-reliance and abundance of rich natural resources such as game, crops and valuable minerals.

The Dale rested in the gorge of River Arkhen, a steep and rocky cliffside that offered natural protection on either side. The only routes into the Dale were the mouth of the valley at Archenbridge and a winding trail at White Ford leading to Highmoon.

Despite their warlike attitude, the dale owed its prosperity to mercantile success rather than military prowess. As such the life of a successful trader and businessman was highly valued.

Lawfulness and order were paramount to achieve continued prosperity in the eyes of the Archendalesmen, a view that was propagated by the Three Swords. As such, adventurers were not necessarily welcomed as they often brought uncertainty and chaos.

entities.name: Archentree
entities.description:
Archentree was less of a settlement and more of an ancestral gathering place for treants of Mielikki's Garden on Ilighôn island off the coast of the Vilhon Reach.

Archentree and the rest of Mielikki's Garden contained a huge number of oak trees. Some speculated that treants seeded the mighty trees, while other sages claimed that the abundance of oaks was what attracted treant to the area.

Archentree was located on a curve of Elder River that flowed from the Elder Spires into the Inner Sea. The House of Silvanus, the main temple of Silvanus in the region ran by the Emerald Enclave was located several miles to the south of Archentree.

Treants that inhabited Mielikki's Garden were old creatures who peered to stay out of business of others. They were likely to ignore pleas for aid or requests to dispense their ancient wisdom by humans. Archentree's treants did not tolerate lit torches often wielded by unwitting visitors and retaliated with swift and deadly efficiency.

entities.name: Arches of Xenosi
entities.description:
The Arches of Xenosi were a ruined path, lined with great arches. They were near the southern end of the Rawlinswood.

The arches framed a tree-lined corridor, which had similar arches every approximately forty or fifty feet; the trees often encroached in the space between the arches, which were themselves covered in ivy and other greenery. Near the entrance, a verdant mist blocked sight further than the approximate distance between arches, also muffling sound. Further along the path, visibility continued to deteriorate, and the forest intruded further into the space lined by the arches.

In , the Talontar blightlord Anammelech ambushed Marrec's party at the entrance of the Arches of Xenosi.

entities.description:
The Archipelago of Altumbel was a collection of islands off the coast of Altumbel, on the Sea of Fallen Stars. The islands were composed of coral and rock, and primarily contained fishing villages. There were numerous wizard towers on the islands, some of which were disused and some of which were still in use. Pirates also occupied the archipelago.

The third largest island in the archipelago.

The second largest island in the archipelago.

The largest of the islands, also known as Vosos.

entities.name: Archive Annex
entities.description:
The Archive Annex was a library found in the city of Neverwinter during the late 15 century DR.

The upper levels of the repository were closed off to many of its patrons, though staff were permitted to retrieve books from within and lend at their discretion.

It was overseen by a stern, blue dragonborn librarian, who belittled some of the library's patrons.

Sometime during or before the , a hill dwarf cleric of Marthammor Duin came into the Archive Annex, looking for more information about an island that appeared to them in a dream.
entities.short_description: The Archive Annex was a library found in the city of Neverwinter during the late 15 century DR.

entities.name: Archive of Curiosities
entities.description:
The Archive of Curiosities was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR.

Unique gifts presented to the Grand Caliph and other treasures were displayed here for the public to see. Some of the more interesting items included a pirate flag taken by the Grand Caliph himself during his adventuring days, a jade throne presented by the emperor of Shou Lung, a magical harp that played music on command, and a large tapestry depicting a king with a purple dragon on his shield.

The Grand Caliph desperately wanted to add a genuine Halruaan skyship to his collection, and was willing to pay handsomely for the acquisition.

entities.name: Archtassel
entities.description:
Archtassel was an unwalled "tassel" (outsiders would call it a village) of Tasseldale.

Woodcutting and trapping were the usual trades in Archtassel. Brethyl fur—fox fur studded with "drops" of clear rock crystal—was produced here and sold in Sembia. The carvers here were famous for their relief-cut doors and wall panels.

entities.name: Arcorar
entities.description:
Arcorar, also known as the Great King Forest, was a large forest region that at one time included the realms/domains of Rystall Wood, Cormanthyr, Elven Court, Jhyrennstar, Semberholme and Uvaeren.

At its largest extent, Arcorar stretched from west of Cormyr to east of the Moonsea.

The forest was originally populated after the Crown Wars when the elves were spreading out looking for new unspoiled regions to settle. Over time, this forest broke up into smaller and smaller pieces until the name was no longer relevant, with the largest remaining fragment being Cormanthor.

entities.name: Arcturiadoom
entities.description:
Arcturiadoom was the 14 level of the massive dungeon known as Undermountain. It served as the personal retreat and doom of Arcturia, a unique lich who was infamous for being one of the most powerful of Halaster Blackcloak's seven apprentices.

Several of the hallways and alcoves were decorated with statues of Arcturia and Halaster himself. While Arcturia thoroughly made the domain her own, many chambers and rooms featured crypts and foundries, holdovers of the old Melairkyn dwarves. Among these was a large iron tankard that weighed over 1,500 lbs (680.4 kg) and several dwarf-sized statues that had escaped arcane transformation.

As Arcturia herself was a master transmuter, her domain contained a great number of traps that were designed to transmogrify and alter the form of any humanoid creature that happened to set them off. They typically came in the form of magical glyphs, inscribed into the domain's floors. While they could be easily dispelled, they had the potential to possibly alter the form of any interlopers to anything from otyughs to gelatinous cubes and even wyverns.

The halls of Arcturiadoom, along the caves outside, were inhabited by several types of creatures and humanoids native to the Underdark. Just outside the front entrance of the archmage's domain, a group of carrion crawlers dwelled within a small garden of luminescent fungi. Giant fire beetles could be found scurrying around the stone floors, and were often thrown together in a large cage to create naturally-powered lanterns.

entities.name: Ardeep
entities.description:
Ardeep was a realm of moon elves founded during the First Flowering, around .

The realm of Ardeep encompassed the area later known as the Ardeep Forest as well as lands north of the River Delimbiyr.

Ardeep was a vassal state of Shantel Othreier at the beginning of the Crown Wars. At the conclusion of the Third Crown War in , Shantel Othreier was conquered by the Vyshaantar Empire of Aryvandaar. Ardeep continued to battle against the forces of Aryvandaar until it was conquered in . It took the next hundred years for Aryvandaar to gain complete control and two of Ardeep's rulers were slain: Ilitharath and his grandson, Tarosspur.

After Shantel Othreier was conquered by the Vyshaantar Empire, it was taken as a vassal realm of the Empire. When the Vyshaan were dissolved, Ardeep joined with Illefarn in . When Aelinthaldaar was razed by its own people in , Illefarn split into three fragmented states of which Ardeep was one and became independent for the first time in many millenia.

entities.name: Ardeep Forest
entities.description:
The Ardeep Forest, also known as the Faraway Forest or Elfwood, was a relatively small but thick woodland in northwest Faerûn. Elven scribes usually compounded the name to "Ardeepforest" in order to denote the forest as opposed to the realm that once encompassed a large part of the Sword Coast.

In the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, the forest was a few miles east of Waterdeep, on the south bank of the River Dessarin. Three clearings in the northwest corner closest to Waterdeep were favorite rendezvous spots for clandestine lovers and runaways. The interior of Ardeep Forest contained many ridges and steep gullies that were hidden beneath thick vines, dense shrubbery, and cloaking mists that presented a danger to casual travelers. In addition, tunnels, cellars, and vaults constructed by dwarves during a time of alliance became pitfalls centuries later.

The forest was once much bigger than the extent shown on maps of the 14–century DR. In the Year of Oaths Forsaken, −626 DR, the trees extended unbroken (except by rivers) from Neverwinter Wood down through Kryptgarden Forest, Ardeep Forest, the Misty Forest, and ended in the Trollbark Forest north of the Troll Hills. Millennia before that, the forest was connected to what eventually became the High Forest.

The dwarvish contributions to the (eventual) hazards of Ardeep Forest were primarily built during the 6–century DR when the kingdom of Phalorm briefly flourished.

entities.name: Ardeep River
entities.description:
The Ardeep River was a river in the Sword Coast North region, a few miles southeast of Waterdeep, between the River Dessarin and the River Delimbiyr.

The river originated in the Ardeep Forest and flowed westward to the Sea of Swords, where it forked into three branches forming a small delta. The northern branch was considered a continuation of the Ardeep River, while the central branch was a creek known as the Selpir and the southernmost branch was known as the South Ardeep River.

The fortified village of Nightstone was located on a fenced island on the Ardeep River, a few miles south of the Ardeep Forest. The river served as a moat to the village, and the area was rich with trout.

entities.description:
The River Ardulith was a river on the island of Evermeet. It flowed into the sea at the island's capital, Leuthilspar, on the east coast. Although it was a large river, its flow was gentle. It was used by elven boats and ships.

entities.name: Arena
entities.description:
The Arena was a coliseum located in the city of Zhentil Keep during the mid–14 century DR before that city's destruction.

The Arena was located in Zhentil Keep's Inner Quarter along the Street of the Gods.

All manners of gladiatorial games were conducted within the Arena. The structure was also used heavily by Zhentil Keep's justice system by having condemned criminals fight to the death Trials of combat were held four or five times per week. There was slim hope for combatants who managed to survive their first contest as they would be summoned to fight again and again until slain. Furthermore, the living conditions for combatants within the Arena cells were deplorable and injured combatants were not given any form of healing.

The Arena was used as a bazaar to unload larger caravans on days where no fights were scheduled.

entities.name: Arena beneath Llorkh
entities.description:
The Arena beneath Llorkh was a fighting pit located under Llorkh in the mid–14 century DR.

The arena was constructed far beneath Llorkh, and one of its tunnel entrances was connected to the Griffon's Grange tavern.

The Arena beneath Llorkh seemed to have a dirt floor that was surrounded by a huge stone observation area. This area had several columns and torches lighting it, as well as a central dais. Steel gratings held the monsters in the preparation areas before fights, and were right next to the arena.

Several small holding cells housed gladiators expected to fight in future battles. Here, the gladiators were only served disgusting slop in metal bowls.

entities.description:
The Arena Efreetum or the Djen Arena was a gladiatorial arena located in the city of Calimport in Calimshan. It and the Arena Sabam were known collectively as the Djen Arenas, a pair of arenas dedicated to entertaining the rulers of the city and the common folk alike and among the most important structures in the City of Slaves. It was half-destroyed in 1479 DR.

A grandiose four-story building, the Arena Efreetum lay in the city's Trades Ward, within the Shomuz Drudach of the Larau Sabban and not far from the Arena Sabam.

Formerly, the Djen Arenas were part of the Games Sabban,

Like slightly larger Sabam, the arena was huge: four stories in height and visible across almost the whole Trades Ward, being seen from atop the sabban walks up to three sabbans distant.

entities.name: Arena of Blood
entities.description:
The infamous Arenas of Blood, also known as the Blood Arenas, were a pair of identical gladiatorial arenas located in the city of Manshaka in Calimshan.

One of the Arenas was located in the northeastern drudach of the northwestern sabban of the city; the other was found in the southern drudach (south of Drudach Street) of the northeastern sabban.

The Arenas were large, circular structures, walled all around and with two levels of stands for spectators. The high walls around the arena bore banners and circular emblems depicting downward-pointing daggers. Huge gates led down to the dungeons beneath.

Beneath each Arena was a labyrinth of passages and tunnels intended to prevent escape, in addition to 100 guards.

The Arena of Games was an open pavilion located in the capital city of Skuld in Mulhorand during the mid–14 century DR..

The Arena was located in the southeast corner of Skuld near the River of Shadows.

The Arena of games was encircled by a grove of trees.

It and the Arena Efreetum were known collectively as the Djen Arenas, a pair of arenas dedicated to entertaining the rulers of the city and the common folk alike and among the most important structures in the City of Slaves.

A grandiose four-story building, the Arena Sabam lay in the city's Trades Ward, within the Mirab Drudach of the Larau Sabban and not far from the Arena Efreetum.

Formerly, the Djen Arenas were part of the Games Sabban, before Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal established the system of wards in the .

Arfinnsheim was a small village located on the island of Norland within the Moonshae Isles.

The village was located along the windward side of the southern end of the North Jotunhammer Mountains near central Norland. Fierce storms rolling in off the Trackless Sea were common in Arfinnsheim given its lack of natural protection.

entities.description:
The Argent Palace was Graz'zt's personal home in the city of Zelatar.

The palace was composed of sixty-six ivory towers and scores and scores of mirrored hallways. The cold but meticulous hallways were filled with wandering bodaks and other more malevolent abyssal denizens as part of the demon lord's amusements. Woe to those residents of Zelatar who received an invitation to an audience with Graz'zt in his palace!

From his palace, Graz'zt planned and schemed his intricate plots to gain more power while thwarting his enemies.

entities.name: Argentil
entities.description:
Argentil was the palace of Selûne, goddess of the moon, in her planar realm known as the Gates of the Moon. It was also inhabited by Finder Wyvernspur, god of art, around 1372 DR.

Lying in the middle of the plane, Argentil was a vast hall fashioned of shining silver. It was a beautiful place, but quiet, where all sound seemed hushed. The ever-present moonlight hugged all beings and things, making them glow with a soft, silvery light.

From the 1370s DR, the hall was adorned all over with the artworks created by Finder's petitioners. His own chambers enjoyed constant music.

By 1479 DR, it was surrounded by Brightwater, the city of Sune, goddess of love.

entities.description:
Argentor was a village of earthsoul genasi located in southern Tethyr within the Mir Spires.

The village's dwellings were hollowed out from the spires by the genasi using their innate ability to shape rock.

In 1479 DR, Argentor was attacked by minotaurs sent by the ruler of Calimport to abduct his long lost son, Cephas, who was traveling with a circus giving a performance at the village.

entities.description:
The Arglander River was one of the major sources of the Deepwash.

The river was located within Ahlarkhem Barony in Erlkazar. It flowed down from the tallest of the High Peaks of the Cloven Mountains into the Deepwash. The river had many cascades and rapids, making it extremely difficult to cross. The only exception was at the Shadebridge.

Argul was a ruined castle located in northern Eskorn, Laerakond.

Argul was built by dragonborn slaves to serve as a lair for the dragon lord Argularragh. Over time, people named the castle after the dragon.

entities.name: Argyr's Realmsry
entities.description:
Argyr's Realmsry was a general store and large warehouse in the village of Dawngleam in Cormyr in the 14 century DR.

This shop carried all manner of goods, imported from the cities of Marsember and Suzail at the order of customers who put down half the price as a deposit. The shop was aided in its intercity acquisitions by agents of the Cormyrean crown, who had an avid interest in ensuring that Dawngleam was on track to develop into a full city.

Some of the daily oddities that it carried included food (such as cheeses), wine, clothes, nails, tools, ropes, furniture, candles, and even the secondhand gowns and gloves of nobles.

Circa 1366 DR, the shop's proprietor, Austas Argyr, spent over a season sending letters to the prominent business woman Aurora. He hoped to convince her to make Argyr's Realmsry into an outlet of the Aurora's Emporium, for he feared that Aurora might be planning to open an outlet in Dawngleam that would compete with his shop. However, Austas would receive no reply from Aurora within that time. His concern drove Austas to diligently provide his customers the best service possible.

entities.name: Ariel-than
entities.description:
Ariel-Than was an elven city in Chondalwood, razed to the ground in 144 DR.

In the winter, early 144 DR, armies of the free-cities of Vilhon Reach invaded the forest of Chondalwood. The city of Ariel-Than was the closest to the edge and was burned to the ground by the invaders. With the dead toll exceeding two thousand, very few elves survived the assault and and retreated deeper into Chondalwood. Some said that the survivors settled in Rucien-Xan, a legendary undiscovered elven city in the heart of Chondalwood.

The destruction of Ariel-Than was the event that created the nation of Chondath.

entities.name: Aris Castle
entities.description:
Castle Aris was the fortified estate of Lord Vorik Aris, a traitorous noble of Cormyr. It was located north-west of Eagle Peak in the far western reaches of Cormyr, on the Tunlands plains beyond the Storm Horns.

It was linked to Wyvernwatch Castle via a permanent portal, which Lord Aris used to move treasure, troops, and himself around without the Crown noticing. The portal archway in Castle Aris had three red gems embedded in it, on the keystone and two pillar bases, with the removal of one deactivating the portal until it was replaced. Removing all three would violently destroy the portal and blast both ends of it with potentially lethal energy.

entities.name: Arita
entities.description:
Arita was a village located in Miyama Province in Kozakura.

Arita, a small village with eigthy-three buildings, was once a serene and prosperous farming community. It served as a vital hub where local peasants could trade their produce downstream and interact with merchants from Okahira. However, recent events have cast a shadow over the village's former tranquility.

The village has fallen under the control of hu hsien from a nearby fortified tower. Shortly after assuming command of the nearby tower, one of the hu hsien infiltrated Arita, assassinated the myoshu, and assumed his role. This impostor, along with his compatriots from the tower, was exploiting the village and its environs, masquerading as rightful authorities.

The villagers, deceived by the guise of legitimacy, have reluctantly accepted the hu hsien's oppressive rule, enduring their increasing demands and injustices. Yet, beneath this veneer of submission, tensions were escalating. The hu hsien's greed grows, even as their plunder yields diminishing returns, pushing the community to its breaking point.
entities.short_description: Arita was a village located in Miyama Province in Kozakura.

entities.name: Arkhen Falls
entities.description:
The Arkhen Falls were the largest and most beautiful waterfall in all of the Dalelands. It was formed by a spring shooting out from Mount Thalagbror, cascading down the southern face of the northern ridge of the Thunder Peaks. The rushing waters emptied out into the gorge of the Arkhen Vale and formed the River Arkhen.

There was a legend that pegasi would flutter around the falls.

The rocky cliffs behind the falls were rich with valuable minerals such as copper and gem stones.

entities.name: Arkhen Vale
entities.description:
The Arkhen Vale was a long valley within Archendale, created by the River Arkhen. Either side of the gorge was beset by steep cliffs leading down into the swift current of the Arkhen.

The Dawnpost road came into the vale from Ordulin, running alongside the River Arkhen until crossing it at the Arkhen Bridge just north of the city of Archenbridge, before extending further south to Daerlun. On the other end of the valley was a road leading north from White Ford,

The valley floor was rich with lush flora such as ferns, mosses and full of small ponds and waterfalls.

entities.name: Arkhen's Invocatorium
entities.description:
Arkhen's Invocatorium was a college of magic in Silverymoon that specialized in sorcery and invocation magic. Once an independent institution, its relocation came with being subsumed into the Conclave of Silverymoon.

The Invocatorium was once situated in a stone fortress, on the east side of Silverymoon's Northbank. It later moved into an entirely new building in the Southbank, between the Lady's College and Miresk's School of Thaumaturgy.

The school took its name from its head teacher, Arkhen the Icy, the Magus Invoker at the Conclave of Silverymoon and later Master Sorcerer. He was an infamously strict teacher.

The second building to call the Invocatorium home full of many furnishings, almost all of whom were animated constructs under the command of Arkhen.

entities.name: River Arkhen
entities.description:
The River Arkhen, also known as the River Elzimmer, down to Selgaunt Bay in Sembia.

The great city of Archenbridge, which also served as Archendale's capital, gained its name from its position straddling the river over the eponymous Arkhen Bridge along the Dawnpost.

The River Arkhen rested in a deep gorge that cut through the Arkhen Vale. It was fed by the Arkhen Falls, which emerged from Mount Thalagbror, in the Thunder Peaks, and continued southeast between the Marching Mountains and the Arch Wood forest.

The original Arkhen Bridge, a stonework crossing which allowed travel over the River Arkhen, was originally erected around 1100 DR by a dwarven engineer by the name of Naiden Stonewright. In 1293 DR, a massive flood of the river destroyed all but its stone casements and the buttresses, A wooden bridge was built in its place, upon the foundation set in by the dwarf almost two centuries before.
